2027-02-02.title: Mayaltho · The Entrance of our Lord into the Temple
readings: The Spirit rests on the shoot of Jesse
Christ entered the Holy Place with his own blood
2027-02-02.alt: Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple (2 February), forty days after Yaldo.
2027-02-02.verse: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation.
theo: Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring the Child to the Temple “to present him to the Lord”, as the Law required for every firstborn son, and they offer the sacrifice of the poor: “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons” (Leviticus 12:8). The Lord of the Temple enters his own house, carried in his mother's arms. Malachi had promised: “the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple” (Malachi 3:1).

There an old man, Simeon, “righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel”, takes the Child in his arms and praises God: “Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.” A whole life of waiting is fulfilled in one embrace.

Then Simeon says to Mary: “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed… and a sword will pierce your own soul too.” Joy and sorrow meet at the Temple door. The Child presented today will offer himself on the Cross. Hebrews says: Christ “entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.”

Mayaltho comes just before the Great Fast. It teaches us to present our lives to God, as Mary and Joseph presented Jesus; to wait faithfully like Simeon and Anna; and to welcome Christ, the light of the nations, into our arms and our hearts.
conn: The Lord comes to his Temple.
Malachi 3:1 is fulfilled: the Lord enters his Temple, not in power but as a child.
The offering of the poor.
Leviticus 12:8: the Holy Family offered two birds, the gift of those who could not afford a lamb. The true Lamb was in Mary's arms.
Without blemish.
Leviticus 22:17–25 requires offerings without blemish; Christ is the spotless offering (1 Peter 1:19; Hebrews 9:14).
Light to the nations.
Simeon's song echoes Isaiah 42:6 and 49:6: the Servant is “a light to the nations”.
altar: Simeon held the Lord in his arms; in Holy Communion we receive him into our hearts. Simeon's song is a fitting prayer after Communion: “Now, Lord, let your servant go in peace; my eyes have seen your salvation.”
outline: Forty days after Yaldo the Child comes to the Temple.
Mary and Joseph give their Son to God. Do we offer our children and our lives?
Faithful waiting in old age; the elderly as witnesses of hope.
Joy and sorrow together: the Child is the sign that will be opposed.
Present yourself to God as Lent begins.
live: Offer your day
Begin each morning this week by presenting your day to God.
Honour the elderly
Visit an elderly person and listen to their memories of faith, as Simeon and Anna would have shared theirs.
Pray Simeon's song
Pray Luke 2:29–32 each night before sleep.
fathers: St Sophronius of Jerusalem
“Let us all hasten to meet him… let us all carry lights… Simeon took him in his arms; let us too embrace him” (Sermon on the Hypapante).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He marvels that the Lord of the Temple was carried into the Temple, and that the old man held the Ancient of Days, who released him in peace (Hymns on the Nativity).
magis: Catechism 529
The presentation of Jesus in the Temple shows him to be the firstborn Son who belongs to the Lord; Simeon and Anna recognise in him the long-expected Messiah.
Catechism 583
Jesus showed deep respect for the Temple, where he was presented forty days after his birth.
Vita Consecrata (on 2 Feb)
The feast of the Presentation is kept in the universal Church as the World Day for Consecrated Life.
saints: 3 Feb: Mar Simon and Morth Hanna (Simeon and Anna). 4 Feb: St John de Britto. 7 Feb: Kothine Sunday; the Great Fast begins.
2027-02-02.prayer: Lord God, your Son was presented in the Temple and received by Simeon and Anna. Accept the offering of our lives; let us wait for you with their faith and welcome you with their joy, and let your Christ be the light of our homes and of all nations. Amen.

2027-02-07.title: Kothine Sunday · First Sunday of the Great Fast
readings: Return to me with all your heart
Is not this the fast that I choose?
In Antioch they were first called Christians
2027-02-07.alt: Kothine Sunday, the miracle at Cana: first Sunday of the Great Fast. The special prayers of the Fast begin this evening; Shubkono, the service of reconciliation, is on Monday 8 February.
2027-02-07.verse: Jesus did this, the first of his signs, in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
theo: The Malankara Church begins the Great Fast with a wedding. On Kothine Sunday we read the miracle at Cana, where Jesus changed water into wine. It may seem strange to start a season of fasting at a feast, but it is deeply wise. The Fast is not about sadness; it is about transformation. The water of our ordinary, tasteless lives can become the wine of God's joy, if we do what Mary says: “Do whatever he tells you.”

The prophets tell us what kind of fast God wants. Joel: “Return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing.” Isaiah: “Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice… to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house?” Fasting from food is meant to open our hearts to God and our hands to the poor.

St Paul shows the inner work of Lent: “Put to death whatever in you is earthly… clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience… Above all, clothe yourselves with love.” The Fast is a change of clothes: putting off the old self and putting on Christ. Acts reminds us that it was in Antioch, the mother Church of our Syriac tradition, that the disciples were first called Christians.

The jars at Cana were filled “up to the brim” with water at Jesus' word. In these fifty days, let us fill our jars: with prayer, fasting, almsgiving and the Word of God. At the end of the Fast, at Qyomtho, Christ will give us the best wine, kept until now: the joy of his Resurrection.
conn: Water into wine.
At Cana water for purification becomes the wine of the wedding feast; the old covenant is fulfilled in the new (John 2:6–10).
The rainbow.
Genesis 9:13: God's covenant after the flood. Lent is a time to return to the covenant God never breaks.
The commandments.
Exodus 20: Lent is a time to examine our lives by the commandments and make a good Confession.
The true fast.
Isaiah 58:6–7 and Joel 2:12–13: fasting with the heart and with the hands.
altar: At Cana Jesus changed water into wine; at the altar he changes wine into his own Blood. Every Holy Qurbono of the Fast is a small Cana, preparing us for the great feast of the Resurrection.
outline: Why does our Lent begin at a wedding?
Water into wine: God changes ordinary lives.
Mary's advice for the whole Fast.
Joel 2 and Isaiah 58: return with the heart, share with the poor.
Prayer, fasting, almsgiving, Scripture; Shubkono and Confession.
live: Make a Lenten plan
Decide as a family: one food to fast from, one daily prayer, one work of charity.
Come to Shubkono
Take part in the service of reconciliation on Monday and ask forgiveness of those you have hurt.
Share your bread (Isaiah 58:7)
Put aside the money saved by fasting for the poor.
fathers: St Ephrem the Syrian
He sings of the Lord who at Cana changed water into wine, and asks him to change our hearts in the same way during the Fast (Hymns on the Fast and on Virginity).
St John Chrysostom
“Do you fast? Give me proof of it by your works… If you see a poor man, take pity on him; if you see an enemy, be reconciled with him” (Homilies on the Statues 3).
magis: Catechism 1434–1439
Interior penance is expressed in fasting, prayer and almsgiving; Lent is a privileged time for it.
Catechism 2043
The precept of fasting and abstinence prepares us for the liturgical feasts.
Catechism 1613
Jesus' presence at Cana confirms the goodness of marriage; the Church sees in it the sign of the new covenant.
saints: 8 Feb (Monday): Shubkono; the Great Fast begins. 10 Feb: anniversary of the establishment of the Syro-Malankara Major Archiepiscopate (2005). 11 Feb: Our Lady of Lourdes, World Day of the Sick.
2027-02-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, at Cana you changed water into wine and revealed your glory. As we begin the Great Fast, change our hearts: teach us to do whatever you tell us, to fast with love, to share with the poor, and to reach with joy the feast of your Resurrection. Amen.

2027-02-14.title: Garbo Sunday · The Healing of the Leper
readings: Naaman is cleansed in the Jordan
They shall seek the Lord their God
Jesus touches and cleanses a leper
2027-02-14.alt: Second Sunday of the Great Fast.
2027-02-14.verse: Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.
theo: The Sundays of the Great Fast in our tradition follow Christ the physician: the leper, the paralytic, the Canaanite woman's daughter, the bent woman, the man born blind. Lent is a season of healing. Today a man “covered with leprosy” falls on his face before Jesus and says: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.” Jesus “stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, ‘I do choose. Be made clean.’ Immediately the leprosy left him.”

Leprosy in the Bible was more than a disease. The leper had to live outside the camp, cry “Unclean!”, and could touch no one. Jesus does what no one would do: he touches him. The Law said that touching a leper made you unclean; with Jesus, the opposite happens: his touch makes the leper clean. This is what Lent offers us: the touch of Christ on the parts of our life we hide from others.

Naaman, the proud Syrian general, was told by Elisha to wash seven times in the Jordan. At first he was angry: was this not too simple? But when he obeyed, “his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.” Healing requires humility. The leper in the Gospel knelt; Naaman went down into the river. In Lent we kneel in confession and go down into the waters of repentance.

Isaiah prays: “O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be our arm every morning, our salvation in the time of trouble.” Jesus himself, after healing the leper, “would withdraw to deserted places and pray.” Healing and prayer go together. Let us bring to Christ in this Fast whatever in us is unclean, and hear him say: “I do choose. Be made clean.”
conn: Naaman and the leper.
Elisha healed a foreigner through the waters of the Jordan; Jesus heals with a touch and a word. Jesus himself recalls Naaman (Luke 4:27).
The ark.
Noah entering the ark (Genesis 7) is an image of salvation through the Church and Baptism (1 Peter 3:20–21).
Outside the camp.
Leviticus 13:45–46 excluded lepers; Christ “suffered outside the city gate” (Hebrews 13:12) to bring the excluded in.
Sin as leprosy.
The Fathers saw leprosy as an image of sin: it spreads, isolates and disfigures; only Christ cleanses.
altar: The leper asked to be touched; in Holy Communion Christ does more than touch us: he enters us. Before Communion we say with the centurion and the leper: Lord, I am not worthy, but only say the word.
outline: The Sundays of Lent: Christ the physician.
Humble, trusting prayer. Jesus always chooses to heal what we bring him.
Jesus touches the untouchable. Who are the “lepers” of our society?
Healing through simple obedience: Confession, prayer, fasting.
Jesus withdrew to pray; make space for prayer in Lent.
live: Make a good Confession
Bring Christ what you hide most; hear the words of absolution as his touch.
Touch the untouchable
Visit or help someone avoided by others: a patient, a migrant worker, a prisoner's family.
Morning prayer (Isaiah 33:2)
Begin each day of the Fast with “O Lord, be our arm every morning.”
fathers: St John Chrysostom

Christ touched the leper to show that he was not under the law but above it, and that to the pure nothing is impure: his hand did not become unclean, but the leprous body became clean (Homilies on Matthew 25).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He calls Christ the Physician who came down to the sick, and asks that the medicine of his mercy heal the hidden sores of the soul (Hymns on the Fast).
magis: Catechism 1503–1505
Christ the physician: his compassion for the sick and his healings are signs that God has visited his people; he takes up our infirmities.
Catechism 1421
The Lord Jesus, physician of our souls and bodies, willed that his Church continue his work of healing in the sacraments of Penance and Anointing.
Message for the World Day of the Sick
The Church cares for the sick as Christ did; read the Pope's annual message (11 February) on vatican.va.
saints: The weekdays of the Great Fast. 22 Feb (next Monday): the Throne of St Peter at Antioch.
2027-02-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, physician of souls and bodies, you touched the leper and made him clean. Stretch out your hand over us in this Fast: cleanse what is hidden, heal what is wounded, and give us the humility of Naaman and the faith of the leper. Amen.

2027-02-21.title: M'shario Sunday · The Healing of the Paralytic
readings: The song of Moses as a witness
They hear your words but do not do them
Woe to those who call evil good
Signs and wonders by the apostles
While we were still sinners, Christ died for us
Four friends lower the paralytic through the roof
2027-02-21.alt: Third Sunday of the Great Fast.
theo: Jesus is teaching in a crowded house in Capernaum. Four men bring a paralysed friend on a mat, but they cannot get near. So they climb onto the roof, dig through it, and lower him down in front of Jesus. Mark says: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’” The faith of the friends opens the way for the sick man.

Everyone expected a healing of the legs. Jesus begins with the heart. The deepest paralysis is sin: it keeps us from walking towards God and towards others. The scribes object: “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” They are right; and that is exactly the point. Jesus then says: “So that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins… stand up, take your mat and go to your home.” The visible healing proves the invisible one.

Ezekiel warns of people who listen to the prophet's words like a lovely song and do nothing: “they hear what you say, but they will not do it.” Isaiah cries: “Ah, you who call evil good and good evil.” The paralysis of the soul often begins there: hearing without doing, calling sin by softer names. Lent is the time to stand up and walk.

St Paul gives the reason for our hope: “God proves his love for us in that while we still were sinners Christ died for us.” We do not have to cure ourselves first. Like the paralytic, we only need to be brought to Jesus, and to let others carry us when we cannot walk.
conn: Carried by faith.
The four friends are an image of the Church: we carry one another to Christ by prayer, intercession and example.
Authority to forgive.
Christ gave this authority to the apostles (John 20:22–23); it continues in the sacrament of Penance.
Hearing and doing.
Ezekiel 33:32 and James 1:22: be doers of the word, not hearers only.
Peter's shadow.
Acts 5:15: the sick are laid on mats in the street so Peter's shadow may fall on them; Christ's healing continues through the Church.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono we are like the paralytic, lowered before the Lord by the prayer of the whole Church. Before Communion the priest prays for the forgiveness of our sins; then the Lord says to us, “Stand up and walk.”
outline: The roof broken open: what would we do to bring a friend to Jesus?
Point 2 · Sin is the deepest paralysis
Ezekiel and Isaiah: honesty about sin.
Confession and a new start; God loved us while we were sinners.
live: Carry a friend
Pray every day this week for one person who cannot or will not come to God.
Do what you hear (Ezekiel 33:32)
Choose one teaching from today's Gospel and act on it this week.
Confession
If you have not yet confessed this Lent, do it this week.
fathers: St Ambrose of Milan
How great is the Lord, who for the merit of some pardons others… If you doubt your own merit, seek the prayers of others; the Church will pray for you (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 5, 11).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He sees in the paralytic the human race, made helpless by sin, which the Physician raised by a word, showing that he who forgives is God (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Catechism 1441–1442
Only God forgives sins; Jesus, the Son of God, exercises this divine power and gives it to his apostles for the Church.
Catechism 1421
Christ, physician of souls and bodies, healed the paralytic and forgave his sins; the Church continues this in Penance.
Catechism 2634–2636
Intercessory prayer: asking on behalf of another, as the four friends did.
saints: 22 Feb: the Throne of St Peter at Antioch. 23 Feb: St Polycarp of Smyrna. 24 Feb: the Finding of the Head of St John the Baptist. 25 Feb: Blessed Rani Maria (as in the 2025–26 lectionary).
2027-02-21.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of four friends and forgave the sins of the paralytic. Forgive our sins, heal the paralysis of our hearts, and make us friends who carry others to you. Raise us up, that we may walk in your ways. Amen.

2027-02-28.title: Knanoitho Sunday · The Canaanite Woman
readings: Thus far the Lord has helped us
A house of prayer for all peoples
2027-02-28.alt: Fourth Sunday of the Great Fast. The middle day of the Fast falls on Wednesday 3 March, when the Cross is erected in the church.
2027-02-28.verse: Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.
theo: A Canaanite woman, a foreigner and a pagan, comes shouting after Jesus: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.” At first Jesus does not answer her. The disciples want her sent away. Jesus says he was sent to the lost sheep of Israel. But she kneels and says: “Lord, help me.” And when Jesus speaks of the children's bread, she replies: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.”

This is one of the most moving prayers in the Gospel. She does not argue about her rights; she does not give up; she accepts being called small, and still trusts. Jesus is amazed: “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” Her daughter is healed from that hour. Jesus' silence was not a refusal; it was a school of persevering faith.

Isaiah had prophesied that foreigners who hold fast to the covenant would be brought to God's holy mountain, “for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.” The Canaanite mother is the first fruit of that promise. The bread meant for the children is enough for all; in the desert God “rained bread from heaven” for the whole people (Exodus 16:4).

St Paul cries out in Romans: “Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord!” The mother's cry and Paul's cry are the same: we cannot save ourselves, but Christ can. Halfway through the Fast, the Church sets up the Cross in the middle of the church: the answer to every cry for help.
conn: A house of prayer for all peoples.
Isaiah 56:7, quoted by Jesus when cleansing the Temple, is fulfilled when a Canaanite woman finds mercy.
Crumbs and the bread from heaven.
The manna (Exodus 16) and the multiplication of loaves just before and after this Gospel (Matthew 14–15) point to the Eucharist, offered to all nations.
Ebenezer.
Samuel's stone “Thus far the LORD has helped us” (1 Samuel 7:12) is the grateful memory of persevering faith.
Pride and humility.
Sirach 10:12–13: pride begins when we forsake the Lord; the woman's humility opens heaven.
altar: The woman asked only for crumbs from the table. At the Holy Qurbono we receive not crumbs but the whole Bread of Life. Let us come with her humility: “Lord, I am not worthy.”
outline: When God seems silent: do we give up?
Silence, refusal, and still she kneels: “Lord, help me.”
She accepts being small and trusts anyway.
Isaiah 56: God's house is for everyone; welcome the stranger.
Mid-Lent: the Cross set up in our church; renew your Lenten resolutions.
live: Don't stop praying
Take up again a prayer you abandoned because God seemed silent.
Pray for your children
Mothers and fathers: bring each child's needs to Jesus by name, like the Canaanite mother.
Welcome a stranger
Show kindness to someone of another background, language or faith this week.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
Christ delayed the gift not to drive her away but to reveal her faith; her persistence made her an example to all the ages (Homilies on Matthew 52).
St Ephrem the Syrian
He praises the mother whose love for her daughter made her bold, and whose humility drew mercy from the Lord of the table (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Catechism 2610
Jesus teaches filial boldness in prayer: “Whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you receive it.” He is amazed at the faith of the Canaanite woman.
Catechism 2742–2745
Persevering prayer; praying without ceasing.
Catechism 543
Everyone is called to enter the Kingdom; announced first to Israel, it is meant for all nations.
saints: 3 Mar (Wednesday): the middle day of the Great Fast; erection of the Cross (Gogultho). 7 Mar: K'piphtho Sunday. 9 Mar: the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste.
2027-02-28.prayer: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. Give us the humble, persevering faith of the Canaanite mother; hear our prayers for our children and families; and make your Church a house of prayer for all peoples. Amen.

2027-02-01.title: Monday after Aneede Sunday
readings: Rescued from darkness into the kingdom of his beloved Son
Pray then in this way: Our Father
2027-02-01.alt: Season of Denho. Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple, is tomorrow; the Great Fast begins next week.
2027-02-01.verse: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
theo: Paul tells the Colossians that he never stops praying for them: “we have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding, so that you may lead lives worthy of the Lord.” He prays that they may be “prepared to endure everything with patience, while joyfully giving thanks to the Father”, and then he names the great change that has already happened: “He has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.” The Christian life is lived in that new kingdom, and it is learned in prayer.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches the prayer of that kingdom: “Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.” Only one petition receives a commentary from the Lord himself, the one about forgiveness: “if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” Our Church prays the Lord’s Prayer at every hour of the Shehimo and before Holy Communion in the Qurbono. In a week the Great Fast will open with Shubkono, the service of mutual forgiveness. This week is the time to say the Our Father slowly and to ask: whom have I still not forgiven? St Cyprian of Carthage wrote that we call God “Father” together, not “my Father”, because we pray as one people and for one another (in substance).
outline: Ask: how many times did you say the Our Father last week, and did you mean the line about forgiveness?
Point 1 · Filled with the knowledge of his will
Point 3 · Forgive as you are forgiven
“Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
live: Pray it slowly (Matthew 6:9)
Say one Our Father today, pausing after each line.
Prepare for Shubkono (Matthew 6:14)
Name one person you need to forgive before the Fast begins, and pray for them.
2027-02-01.prayer: Our Father in heaven, you rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of your beloved Son. Fill us with the knowledge of your will, teach us to pray as he taught us, and give us hearts that forgive, so that we may enter the Great Fast reconciled with you and with one another. Amen.
altar: Before Holy Communion we pray the Our Father together: forgiven and forgiving, we approach the one Bread.

2027-02-03.title: Wednesday after Aneede Sunday · Mar Shem'on and Morth Hanna
readings: Simeon and Anna meet the child in the temple
2027-02-03.alt: Season of Denho. The day after Mayaltho the Church honours the aged Simeon and the prophet Anna.
2027-02-03.verse: At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
theo: Yesterday we kept Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple. Today our Church turns to the two old people who were waiting there. Simeon “was righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit rested on him.” He had been promised “that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Messiah,” and he came into the temple “guided by the Spirit.” Beside him is Anna, “of a great age”, a widow of eighty-four who “never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.” When she saw the child, “she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.” Long waiting did not make them bitter; it made them ready.

Paul's prayer to the Ephesians shows what such a life is built on. He bows his knees before the Father and prays “that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love,” so that we may “know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.” Simeon and Anna were rooted in that love long before they held it in their arms. Our Church calls them Mar Shem'on and Morth Hanna and keeps them close to the feast. An ancient antiphon of the Church says that the old man carried the child, but the child was guiding the old man (in substance). On this day we thank God for the grandparents and elders of our parishes, whose prayer holds up more than we know.
outline: Ask: who taught you to pray, and how old were they?
Simeon waits and is not disappointed.
Point 2 · Fasting and prayer night and day
Anna, the first to speak of the child.
Point 3 · Rooted and grounded in love
Paul's prayer for the inner self.
“She came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child.”
live: Honour an elder (Luke 2:36–37)
Visit or call an elderly person today and ask them to pray for you.
Speak of the child (Luke 2:38)
Tell someone today one thing Jesus has done for you.
2027-02-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, Light of the nations, you came into the temple and were welcomed by Simeon and Anna. Through their prayers give us patient and faithful hearts, rooted and grounded in love. Bless the grandparents and elders of our families and parishes, and let their long prayer bear fruit in us. Amen.
altar: Simeon took the child in his arms; in the Holy Qurbono the same Lord is placed in our hands and on our lips.

2027-02-04.title: Thursday after Aneede Sunday · St John de Britto
readings: I am not ashamed of the gospel
2027-02-04.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of St John de Britto, priest and martyr of the Madurai mission (1693).
2027-02-04.verse: For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
theo: Paul writes to a Church he has never visited, and he tells them why he longs to come: “I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish, hence my eagerness to proclaim the gospel to you also who are in Rome.” The gospel is not his property but a debt he owes to everyone. And then the great sentence: “For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith.” In the Gospel Jesus is frank about the cost: “the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and there are few who find it.” The narrow gate is not a door for a chosen few; it is the shape of Christ himself, through whom everyone may enter, but only by leaving behind what does not fit.

Our Church today remembers a man who lived both readings in South India. John de Britto was born in Lisbon in 1647 to a noble family and entered the Society of Jesus. He asked to be sent to the Madurai mission, and from the 1670s he lived among the Tamil people as a pandaram, a poor ascetic teacher, walking barefoot, eating simple food and speaking Tamil. The people called him Arul Anandar. He was arrested and beaten more than once, and was finally beheaded at Oriyur in the Marava country on 4 February 1693, after the conversion of a local chief, Thadiya Thevar, had stirred deep opposition. Pius XII canonized him in 1947. He was a debtor to the poor and to the learned of our land, and he was not ashamed of the gospel.
outline: Ask: when were you last embarrassed to show that you are a Christian?
The gospel is a debt we owe.
The power of God for salvation.
“I am not ashamed of the gospel.”
live: Pay your debt (Romans 1:14)
Share one word of faith today with someone who does not know Christ well.
Choose the narrow road (Matthew 7:13–14)
Refuse one easy dishonesty today, even if it costs you.
2027-02-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the narrow gate that leads to life. Through the prayers of St John de Britto, who gave his life for you among the Tamil people, make us unashamed of your gospel, generous to all, and faithful on the hard road that leads to you. Bless the Churches of Tamil Nadu and all who proclaim you in India. Amen.
altar: The martyrs of India offered their lives with Christ; in the Holy Qurbono we offer ours with his one sacrifice.

2027-02-05.title: Friday after Aneede Sunday
readings: Written down to instruct us; God is faithful
If the world hates you, it hated me first
2027-02-05.verse: If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.
theo: Paul looks back at Israel in the wilderness. They had every gift: “our ancestors were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea… and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.” Yet “God was not pleased with most of them.” They desired evil, worshipped idols, tested the Lord and grumbled. “These things happened to them to serve as an example, and they were written down to instruct us.” Baptism and the Eucharist are not a charm that saves us without our cooperation. “So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall.” And at once Paul adds the comfort: “God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out so that you may be able to endure it.”

In the Gospel Jesus prepares his friends for another kind of testing, the hostility of the world: “If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you… Servants are not greater than their master. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you.” The disciples are hated not for their faults but because they belong to him: “I have chosen you out of the world.” On this Friday, the day of the Cross, we remember Christians in India and across the world who suffer for the name of Jesus. As the Great Fast approaches, Paul's warning and Jesus' promise belong together: watch, because you can fall; take heart, because God is faithful and Christ has gone ahead of you. St John Chrysostom says that Paul names the way out together with the trial, so that no one may despair (in substance).
outline: Ask: can a baptized person who receives Communion still fall away?
Point 1 · Written down to instruct us
The servant shares the master's road.
“It hated me before it hated you.”
live: Watch your step (1 Corinthians 10:12)
Name one habit that could make you fall, and plan how to avoid it during the Fast.
Stand with the persecuted (John 15:20)
Pray today for Christians who suffer for their faith, and learn about one such community.
2027-02-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, you were hated without a cause and you went before us on the way of the Cross. Keep us watchful so that we do not fall, and faithful when we are tested. Strengthen all who suffer for your name today, and give them the way out that you have promised. Amen.
altar: Israel drank from the rock, and the rock was Christ; in the Holy Qurbono we drink from his side the true spiritual drink.

2027-02-06.title: Saturday after Aneede Sunday
readings: Rich in good works, generous and ready to share
The rich fool: rich toward God
2027-02-06.alt: Season of Denho. Tomorrow is Kothine Sunday, the first Sunday of the Great Fast, and Catholicos Day.
2027-02-06.verse: So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.
theo: Jesus tells a story about a successful farmer. “The land of a rich man produced abundantly,” and he has a problem every farmer would like to have: no room for the harvest. So he plans: “I will pull down my barns and build larger ones… And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry.” He talks only to himself; there is no God in his plan and no neighbour. “But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’” Jesus does not condemn the harvest. He condemns the barn that has no door to the poor: “So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.”

Paul gives Timothy the positive side of the same teaching. The rich are not to be haughty, nor “to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment. They are to do good, to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share,” and so “take hold of the life that really is life.” This is the last Saturday before the Great Fast. Fasting without almsgiving would only fill a different barn. St Basil the Great, preaching on this parable, said that the bread we store belongs to the hungry and the coat in our chest belongs to the one who has none (in substance). Tomorrow, Catholicos Day, our Church asks every parish to share for the needs of the whole Church; it is a good place to begin being rich toward God.
outline: Ask: if your life were demanded of you tonight, whose would your things be?
Point 2 · You fool, this very night
A plan with no God and no neighbour.
live: Open the barn (Luke 12:21)
Set aside a fixed portion of your money for the poor for the whole Fast.
Share with the Church (1 Timothy 6:18)
Give generously at tomorrow's Catholicos Day collection.
2027-02-06.prayer: Lord God, you richly provide us with everything. Free us from hoping in uncertain riches and from barns built only for ourselves. Make us rich in good works, generous and ready to share, so that we may take hold of the life that really is life. Bless our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our whole Church as we begin the Great Fast. Amen.
altar: At the altar we bring bread and wine, gifts God first gave us, and he returns them as the Bread of life for all.

2027-02-08.title: Monday of the first week of the Great Fast · Shubkono
readings: Forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you
2027-02-08.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), first week. Shubkono, the service of mutual forgiveness, opens the Great Fast. The fast begins today.
2027-02-08.verse: and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.
theo: Today the fast begins, and our Church opens it not with food rules but with forgiveness. In Shubkono, the service of reconciliation, the priest bows before the people and asks their pardon, and the faithful ask pardon of one another before they begin the forty days together. Paul gives the words for it: “Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and do not make room for the devil… Put away from you all bitterness and wrath and anger and wrangling and slander, together with all malice, and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.” A fast kept with an unforgiving heart is only hunger.

The first reading of the Fast is about Abram's faith. Childless and old, he hears: “Do not be afraid, Abram, I am your shield; your reward shall be very great.” God brings him outside: “Look toward heaven and count the stars… So shall your descendants be.” And “he believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness.” The Gospel shows Jesus in the wilderness, fasting forty days and forty nights and answering the tempter three times from the Scriptures: “One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.” This is the shape of our Fast: trust like Abram, peace with one another, and the word of God as our food. St John Chrysostom asks: do you fast? Then show it by your works; let not only the mouth fast, but also the eye, the ear, the hands and the feet (in substance).
outline: Ask: what is harder, giving up food or forgiving one person?
Abram believes and is reckoned righteous.
“Forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”
live: Make peace before sunset (Ephesians 4:26)
Ask or give forgiveness today to one person before the sun goes down.
Feed on the word (Matthew 4:4)
Read one chapter of a Gospel each day of the Fast.
2027-02-08.prayer: Lord Jesus, you fasted forty days in the wilderness and overcame the tempter by the word of God. As we begin the Great Fast, take away all bitterness, anger and malice from our hearts. Make us kind, tenderhearted and forgiving, as the Father has forgiven us in you, and give us the faith of Abram, who believed your promise. Amen.
altar: Reconciled with one another in Shubkono, we come to the altar where Christ reconciles us all to the Father.

2027-02-09.title: Tuesday of the first week of the Great Fast
readings: The covenant sacrifice: Abram keeps watch
No condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus
2027-02-09.verse: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
theo: Abram has believed, but he still asks: “O Lord God, how am I to know that I shall possess it?” God does not scold him. He asks for a sacrifice: a heifer, a goat, a ram, a turtledove and a pigeon. Abram cuts the animals in two and waits, and “when birds of prey came down on the carcasses, Abram drove them away.” Then darkness falls, and God speaks of the long road ahead: his descendants will be strangers and slaves for four hundred years, and then come out free. Faith is not the end of questions; it is staying beside the sacrifice and driving away whatever would snatch it. In the Fast our prayer, fasting and almsgiving are such an offering, and the birds of prey are many: distraction, discouragement, the voice that says it is useless.

Paul tells us why we can keep watch without fear: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.” The Fast is not an attempt to earn God's love by our own strength; it is letting the Spirit who dwells in us set our minds “on the things of the Spirit”, which are “life and peace.” And in the Gospel Jesus shows whose sacrifice saves us: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.” Unlike the hired hand, he does not run when the wolf comes. He knows his own, and he will bring the other sheep too, “so there will be one flock, one shepherd.” St Gregory the Great says that the Good Shepherd first did what he taught: he laid down his life (in substance).
outline: Ask: have you ever believed God and still wanted a sign?
Point 1 · Driving away the birds of prey
“The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
live: Guard your offering (Genesis 15:11)
Name the one distraction that most steals your prayer, and drive it away today.
Set your mind on the Spirit (Romans 8:6)
Spend ten quiet minutes today with the Gospel of the day.
2027-02-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you laid down your life for us and took away our condemnation. Pour your Spirit into our hearts, so that we may keep watch over the offering of this Fast and drive away all that would steal it. Gather all your sheep into one flock, and keep us close to your voice. Amen.
altar: The Good Shepherd who laid down his life feeds his flock at the altar with his own Body and Blood.

2027-02-10.title: Wednesday of the first week of the Great Fast · Anniversary of the Syro-Malankara Major Archiepiscopal Church
readings: A flaming torch passes between the pieces
I press on toward the goal
But who do you say that I am?
2027-02-10.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), first week. Anniversary of the raising of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church to a Major Archiepiscopal Church (10 February 2005).
2027-02-10.verse: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Messiah of God.”
theo: The covenant with Abram is sealed in the dark: “When the sun had gone down and it was dark, a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between these pieces. On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram.” Only God passes between the halves of the sacrifice; Abram does nothing but watch. In the ancient custom, those who passed between the pieces bound themselves to keep the covenant. Here God binds himself alone. The promise rests on his faithfulness, not ours. Paul, who knew that faithfulness, still says: “Not that I have already obtained this or have already reached the goal; but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own… forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.” The Fast is that pressing on.

In the Gospel Jesus is praying alone and asks his disciples: “Who do the crowds say that I am?” Then the question that matters: “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answers: “The Messiah of God.” Today our Church gives thanks for its own place in that confession. On 10 February 2005 Pope John Paul II raised the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church to the rank of a Major Archiepiscopal Church, with Moran Mor Cyril Baselios as its first Major Archbishop; it is now led by Moran Mor Baselios Cardinal Cleemis, Major Archbishop-Catholicos. A Church that came home to communion with the See of Peter in 1930 was recognised as a Church with its own head and synod within that communion. The torch of God's faithfulness has passed through our history; we press on, confessing with Peter that Jesus is the Messiah of God.
outline: Ask: if Jesus asked you today, “Who do you say that I am?”, what would you answer?
Point 1 · The torch between the pieces
God binds himself to his promise.
“But who do you say that I am?”
live: Confess him (Luke 9:20)
Write down in one sentence who Jesus is for you, and pray it today.
Press on (Philippians 3:13)
Let go of one past failure that keeps you from going forward in the Fast.
2027-02-10.prayer: Lord God, faithful to your covenant, you passed through the darkness to bind yourself to Abram and his children. We thank you for our Syro-Malankara Catholic Church and for the gift of its Major Archiepiscopal dignity in communion with the Successor of Peter. Bless our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and our Holy Synod. Help us to press on toward the goal, confessing that Jesus is the Messiah of God. Amen.
altar: In every Holy Qurbono we pray for the Pope of Rome and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos: one confession of faith, one Body of Christ.

2027-02-11.title: Thursday of the first week of the Great Fast · Our Lady of Lourdes
readings: Sarai, Hagar and a plan made without God
Your life is hidden with Christ in God
2027-02-11.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), first week. Memory of Our Lady of Lourdes; World Day of the Sick.
2027-02-11.verse: for he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant. Surely, from now on all generations will call me blessed;
theo: The reading from Genesis is painful and honest. Sarai, childless, decides to help God keep his promise in her own way: “go in to my slave-girl; it may be that I shall obtain children by her.” Abram agrees. Hagar conceives, contempt grows, Sarai blames Abram, and Abram washes his hands: “Your slave-girl is in your power; do to her as you please.” Sarai deals harshly with her, and the Egyptian slave runs away into the wilderness. A plan made without waiting on God ends with a household broken and the weakest person paying the price. Paul points to the opposite way: “seek the things that are above, where Christ is… Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth, for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.”

The Gospel is Mary's song, the prayer of one who waited on God and let him act: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior, for he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant… He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly.” On 11 February 1858, at the grotto of Massabielle near Lourdes, the Blessed Virgin appeared to Bernadette Soubirous, a poor and sickly girl of fourteen, the first of eighteen apparitions. On 25 March she named herself: “I am the Immaculate Conception.” At her word a spring was uncovered, and the sick have come to it ever since. Because of this, St John Paul II made 11 February the World Day of the Sick. Today the Lord again looks with favour on the lowly: on Hagar in the wilderness, on Bernadette, and on every sick person who prays to him with Mary.
outline: Ask: have you ever tried to make God's promise come true in your own way?
Point 1 · A plan made without God
Seek the things that are above.
Point 3 · He lifted up the lowly
Mary's song, Bernadette and the sick.
“He has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant.”
live: Visit the sick (Luke 1:52)
Visit, call or pray by name for a sick person today.
Wait on God (Colossians 3:2)
Bring one decision you are rushing to God in prayer before acting.
2027-02-11.prayer: Holy Mother of God, Our Lady of Lourdes, you sang that the Lord looks with favour on the lowly. Pray for the sick, the suffering and those who care for them. Teach us to seek the things that are above, to wait on God instead of forcing our own plans, and to magnify the Lord in every circumstance. Lord Jesus, through her prayers heal us in body and soul. Amen.
altar: Mary magnified the Lord with her whole life; in the Holy Qurbono we join her song as we receive her Son.

2027-02-12.title: Friday of the first week of the Great Fast
readings: The God who sees Hagar in the wilderness
The law written on their hearts
Everyone who acknowledges me before others
2027-02-12.verse: And I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God;
theo: Yesterday Hagar ran away into the wilderness. Today “the angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness” and asks two questions that every soul in the Fast should hear: “Hagar, slave-girl of Sarai, where have you come from and where are you going?” She can answer only the first: “I am running away.” God sends her back, but not empty: he promises her a son and names him Ishmael, “for the Lord has given heed to your affliction.” And Hagar, the foreign slave whom no one else noticed, does what almost no one else in Scripture dares: she gives God a name of her own: “You are El-roi,” the God who sees. “Have I really seen God and remained alive after seeing him?” On a Friday of the Fast we remember that the God who sees is the God who looked down from the Cross on all the afflicted.

Paul says that God sees the heart of every human being, not only of those who have the written law: Gentiles “show that what the law requires is written on their hearts, to which their own conscience also bears witness,” on the day “when, according to my gospel, God, through Jesus Christ, will judge the secret thoughts of all.” The Fast is a time to let that light into our secret thoughts. In the Gospel Jesus asks for courage in the open: “everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God.” When we are brought before authorities, we need not worry: “the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.” The God who sees Hagar in the wilderness also stands beside those who confess him before the world.
outline: Ask: where have you come from, and where are you going?
The Spirit will teach you what to say.
live: Answer Hagar's question (Genesis 16:8)
Tonight write two lines: where have I come from in my life, and where am I going?
Examine your conscience (Romans 2:15)
Make an honest examination of conscience today and plan a good confession during the Fast.
2027-02-12.prayer: Lord, you are the God who sees. You found Hagar by the spring in the wilderness and heard her affliction. See us in our wilderness, search our secret thoughts, and heal what you find there. Give us courage to acknowledge your Son before others, and teach us by your Holy Spirit what to say. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Lord who sees our affliction offers himself on the altar for all, near and far.

2027-02-13.title: Saturday of the first week of the Great Fast · Mar Aprem and Mar Theodore; Prophet Haggai
readings: Walk before me, and be blameless
The word of God is living and active
2027-02-13.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), first week. Special remembrance of Mar Aprem (St Ephrem) and Mar Theodore the martyr; commemoration of the Prophet Haggai.
2027-02-13.verse: Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
theo: Abram is ninety-nine when God appears again: “I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be blameless.” God changes his name: “No longer shall your name be Abram, but your name shall be Abraham; for I have made you the ancestor of a multitude of nations.” The covenant is “an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your offspring after you.” A new name means a new life lived in God's sight. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us how God shapes that life: “the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword… it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.” And Jesus, closing the Sermon on the Mount, says that hearing is not enough: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father.” The wise build on rock by doing what they hear; the foolish build on sand, “and great was its fall!”

On this first Saturday of the Great Fast our Church remembers Mar Aprem, St Ephrem the Syrian. Born at Nisibis about 306, he served as a deacon there and later at Edessa, where he died in 373. He taught the faith through hymns sung by choirs, and our liturgy is full of his voice; he is called the Harp of the Spirit, and Pope Benedict XV declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1920. The prayer that bears his name is prayed throughout Lent in many Churches: O Lord and Master of my life, take from me the spirit of sloth, despair, lust of power and idle talk; give me the spirit of chastity, humility, patience and love. With him we remember Mar Theodore, a soldier who chose to die rather than deny Christ in the persecution of the early fourth century, and the Prophet Haggai, who told a people living in comfortable houses to rebuild the ruined house of God. Ephrem in the word, Theodore in his blood, Haggai in rebuilding: each built on rock.
outline: Ask: what is your house built on, the words you say or the words you live?
The word that judges the heart.
“Hears these words of mine and acts on them.”
live: Pray the prayer of St Ephrem (Hebrews 4:12)
Pray it slowly every day of the Fast, with a bow at each petition.
Rebuild (Haggai 1:4)
Give some time or help to your parish church this week.
2027-02-13.prayer: Lord God Almighty, you called Abram to walk before you and gave him a new name. Let your living word search our hearts in this Fast. Through the prayers of Mar Aprem, the Harp of the Spirit, of Mar Theodore the martyr and of the Prophet Haggai, take from us the spirit of sloth, despair, lust of power and idle talk, and give us the spirit of chastity, humility, patience and love, so that we may build our lives on the rock of your word. Amen.
altar: Mar Aprem sang that in the Bread we eat the Fire and the Spirit (in substance); in the Holy Qurbono that living Word becomes our food.

2027-02-15.title: Monday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: The sign of the covenant in the flesh
Devote yourselves to prayer; let your speech be gracious
Do not worry; strive first for the kingdom
2027-02-15.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), second week. Anniversary of the episcopal ordination of Mathews Mar Pachomios (2024).
2027-02-15.verse: But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
theo: The second week of the Fast opens with a hard sign. God tells Abraham: “This is my covenant, which you shall keep, between me and you and your offspring after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised… and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.” The covenant was not only an idea in Abraham's head; it was cut into the body of every man in his household, from the eight-day-old child to the slave bought with money. God wanted his people to carry his promise in their own flesh. Moses would later say what the sign pointed to: “the Lord your God will circumcise your heart.” And Paul tells the Colossians that in Christ they “were circumcised with a spiritual circumcision”, in baptism. The Fast is the time to let God finish that work: to cut away from the heart what does not belong to the covenant.

Paul shows what a marked life looks like in ordinary days: “Devote yourselves to prayer, keeping alert in it with thanksgiving… Conduct yourselves wisely toward outsiders, making the most of the time. Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt.” A fast that sours our speech has missed its point. And Jesus takes away the worry that eats at a fasting heart: “do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink… Look at the birds of the air… Consider the lilies of the field.” We give up some food in Lent partly to learn this: that “your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.” So “strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.” St John Chrysostom says that Jesus does not forbid work, only anxiety; he wants us to sow and labour while trusting the Father who feeds the birds (in substance). Today we also pray for Mathews Mar Pachomios on the anniversary of his episcopal ordination.
outline: Ask: what do you carry on your body that shows whom you belong to?
Point 1 · A sign in the flesh
The covenant cut into Abraham's household.
Point 3 · Strive first for the kingdom
The birds, the lilies and the Father who knows.
“Strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
live: Salt your speech (Colossians 4:6)
For one day, before you speak in anger or complaint, count to five and choose a gracious word.
Hand over one worry (Matthew 6:34)
Write down the worry that most troubles you this week, place it before the Lord in prayer, and do today's work without carrying tomorrow's.
2027-02-15.prayer: Heavenly Father, you made a covenant with Abraham and marked his people as your own. Circumcise our hearts in this Fast, and cut away whatever keeps us from loving you. Teach us to pray with thanksgiving, to speak with grace, and to seek first your kingdom, trusting that you know all we need. Bless Mathews Mar Pachomios and all the shepherds of your Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive the sign of the new covenant, not cut into our flesh but given in the Body and Blood of Christ.

2027-02-16.title: Tuesday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Sarah shall be her name; Isaac is promised
By grace you have been saved through faith
You will know them by their fruits
2027-02-16.verse: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
theo: God now turns to Sarai: “you shall not call her Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name. I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her.” And the father of believers falls on his face and laughs: “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?” Then he makes a quieter, more human prayer: “O that Ishmael might live in your sight!” He already has a son; perhaps he would settle for that. God's answer is both firm and tender: “No, but your wife Sarah shall bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac.” Isaac means “he laughs”: God will turn Abraham's doubtful laugh into the laughter of joy. And Ishmael is not forgotten: “As for Ishmael, I have heard you; I will bless him.” God's plan is larger than our hopes, and kinder than our fears.

Paul tells the Ephesians that every Christian life begins the way Isaac's did: with something impossible that only God can do. “You were dead through the trespasses and sins in which you once lived… But God, who is rich in mercy, out of the great love with which he loved us even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ.” Our fasting does not buy this life: “by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.” Yet grace is not idle: “we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works.” That is why Jesus gives a simple test: “You will know them by their fruits… every good tree bears good fruit.” St Augustine says that when God crowns our merits he is crowning his own gifts (in substance). In the Fast we do not try to grow fruit by our own strength; we stay grafted to the One who makes the tree good.
outline: Ask: have you ever laughed at something God promised because it seemed impossible?
Sarah's new name and Isaac's promise.
Dead in trespasses, made alive with Christ.
“By grace you have been saved through faith.”
live: Thank God for one undeserved gift (Ephesians 2:8)
Write down three gifts in your life you did nothing to earn, and thank God for each tonight.
Look at your fruit (Matthew 7:17)
Ask someone close to you which good fruit they see in your life, and which they would like to see.
2027-02-16.prayer: God rich in mercy, you gave Abraham a son when it was impossible and turned his laughter of doubt into the laughter of joy. You made us alive with Christ when we were dead in our sins. Let us never forget that all is your gift. Make us good trees, rooted in your grace, bearing the fruit of good works which you prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive grace upon grace, the gift we could never earn: Christ himself, who makes us alive.

2027-02-17.title: Wednesday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom
The Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head
2027-02-17.verse: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
theo: Twice in five verses Genesis repeats the same words: “that very day.” Abraham “circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very day, as God had said to him… That very day Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised.” He was ninety-nine years old. He did not form a committee or wait for a more convenient season. God spoke, and Abraham obeyed the same day, beginning with himself and then with all his household. Delay is one of the quiet enemies of the Fast. We mean to pray more, to make our confession, to be reconciled, to give alms; and the days slip by. The Psalmist prays the opposite: “I hurry and do not delay to keep your commandments.”

In the Gospel two men approach Jesus. The first is eager: “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.” Jesus tells him the cost: “Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.” The second wants to follow, but later: “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” Jesus answers: “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.” St John Chrysostom explains that the Lord was not teaching contempt for parents; he was teaching that nothing, not even the most honourable duty, may be placed before following him (in substance). Why is he worth it? Paul gives the answer: in Christ “are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” Paul struggles in prayer so that the hearts of the Colossians may be “encouraged and united in love,” and he rejoices to see “the firmness of your faith in Christ.” The one who has no place to lay his head is himself the treasure.
outline: Ask: what have you been meaning to do for God, but keep postponing?
live: Do it today (Genesis 17:26)
Take one good resolution of this Fast that you have postponed and do it before the day ends.
Seek the treasure (Colossians 2:3)
Spend fifteen minutes today reading the Gospel slowly, as someone searching for treasure.
2027-02-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you had nowhere to lay your head, yet in you are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. Give us the promptness of Abraham, who obeyed that very day. Free us from excuses and delays, unite our hearts in love, and make our faith firm, so that we may follow you wherever you go. Amen.
altar: The Son of Man who had nowhere to lay his head makes his dwelling among us on the altar, and in us when we receive him.

2027-02-18.title: Thursday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Abraham welcomes three guests at Mamre
We are the temple of the living God
The wedding banquet and the wedding robe
2027-02-18.verse: For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, “I will live in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
theo: “The Lord appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.” Three men stand near him, and the old man runs: “he ran from the tent entrance to meet them, and bowed down to the ground… Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree. Let me bring a little bread.” He promises a little and gives a feast: cakes from three measures of choice flour, a calf “tender and good,” curds and milk, and he himself stands by them under the tree while they eat. The Fathers read this scene with wonder. St Ambrose says that Abraham saw three and worshipped one (in substance), and the Church has seen in the three guests at Mamre a foreshadowing of the Holy Trinity, painted in the famous icon of the three angels at table. The God who will one day be revealed as Father, Son and Holy Spirit came first as a guest to an old man's tent.

Paul turns the picture around: now it is God who makes his home in us. “We are the temple of the living God; as God said, ‘I will live in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.’” A temple cannot be shared with idols, and so he warns: “Do not be mismatched with unbelievers… what fellowship is there between light and darkness?” He is not telling us to despise anyone, but not to yoke our hearts to what is opposed to Christ. And in the Gospel God is the host: a king gives a wedding banquet for his son, and when the invited guests make light of it, he fills the hall from the streets, “both good and bad.” Yet one guest has no wedding robe. St Gregory the Great says that the wedding garment is charity: we may be inside the Church and still lack love (in substance). On this Thursday, the day of the Lord's Supper, we prepare the robe of love for the banquet of the altar.
outline: Ask: when a guest comes to your house, what do you hurry to do?
Point 2 · The temple of the living God
God makes his home in us.
Invited by grace, clothed in love.
“We are the temple of the living God.”
live: Welcome a guest (Genesis 18:2)
This week, invite someone who is alone to share a meal with your family, and serve them as Abraham did.
Put on the robe (Matthew 22:12)
Before your next Holy Qurbono, make peace with anyone you are at odds with, so that you come clothed in love.
2027-02-18.prayer: Lord God, you visited Abraham at Mamre as a guest, and he ran to welcome you. Make us generous to every guest and stranger. Dwell in us as in your temple, and keep our hearts free from every idol. You invite us to the wedding feast of your Son; clothe us in the robe of charity, so that we may not be found unworthy at your table. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The guest whom Abraham served at Mamre becomes our host at the altar, inviting good and bad alike to the wedding banquet of his Son.

2027-02-19.title: Friday of the second week of the Great Fast · Mar Ishaq
readings: Sarah laughs: is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
The surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord
No one will snatch them out of my hand
2027-02-19.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), second week. Remembrance of Mar Ishaq; anniversary of the episcopal ordination of Joseph Mar Thomas (2005).
2027-02-19.verse: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord? At the set time I will return to you, in due season, and Sarah shall have a son.
theo: The guests at Mamre ask a strange question: “Where is your wife Sarah?” She is “in the tent,” listening behind the entrance, and when she hears that she will have a son, she laughs to herself: “After I have grown old, and my husband is old, shall I have pleasure?” It is the laugh of a woman who has waited too long and stopped hoping. The Lord hears the laugh that no one saw, and asks: “Why did Sarah laugh?… Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?” Then a small, almost humorous exchange: “But Sarah denied, saying, ‘I did not laugh’; for she was afraid. He said, ‘Oh yes, you did laugh.’” God does not punish her for it. He simply keeps his word. Many of us carry a hidden laugh like Sarah's, a quiet disbelief that God can still do anything new in our lives. The Fast is a time to let him name it, and to hear again: nothing is too wonderful for the Lord.

On this Friday Paul shows where real hope is found: “I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I regard them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ.” He wants to know “the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings by becoming like him in his death.” St Ignatius of Antioch, on his way to martyrdom, wrote that it was better for him to die for Christ than to reign over the ends of the earth (in substance). This is not a love of loss for its own sake; it is the discovery that Christ is worth more than everything. And Christ holds those who belong to him: “My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me. I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand.” Today we also remember Mar Ishaq, and we pray for Joseph Mar Thomas on the anniversary of his episcopal ordination.
outline: Ask: is there a promise of God you have quietly stopped believing?
Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
“Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?”
live: Name your hidden laugh (Genesis 18:12)
Tell God honestly in prayer where you have stopped hoping, and ask him to renew your faith.
Count it as loss (Philippians 3:8)
On this Friday, give up one comfort and spend the time before a crucifix.
2027-02-19.prayer: Lord God, nothing is too wonderful for you. You heard Sarah's hidden laugh and still kept your promise. Heal our quiet disbelief. Give us the heart of Paul, who counted everything as loss for the surpassing value of knowing Christ. Keep us in the hand of your Son, from which no one can snatch us. Bless Joseph Mar Thomas and all our bishops. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: On the altar the one who shared our sufferings and death gives us the power of his resurrection.

2027-02-20.title: Saturday of the second week of the Great Fast
readings: Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
The goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also
2027-02-20.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), second week. Tomorrow is M'shario Sunday, the Sunday of the healing of the paralytic.
2027-02-20.verse: Do not be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
theo: As the guests leave Mamre, Abraham walks with them “to set them on their way,” and the Lord speaks almost to himself: “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?” God treats Abraham as a friend, someone who may know his plans. And he explains why he chose him: “that he may charge his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing righteousness and justice.” Faith is meant to be handed on at home, from parents to children, in words and in the way a household lives. Then God speaks of “the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah.” The cry of those who suffer injustice rises to heaven, and God says: “I must go down and see.” The God of Abraham is not indifferent to the cry of the oppressed.

Paul reminds Titus how a Christian household should look to its neighbours: “to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show every courtesy to everyone.” He does not pretend we were always so: “we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray… But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.” In the Gospel Jesus speaks tenderly to that small, renewed household: “Do not be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom. Sell your possessions, and give alms… For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” St Augustine urged his people to move their treasure to heaven through the hands of the poor, so that their hearts would follow (in substance). Almsgiving in the Fast is not only charity; it is moving our heart to where God is.
outline: Ask: where does your mind go when you are not thinking of anything in particular?
Charging his household to keep the way of the Lord.
Saved by mercy, renewed by the Spirit.
“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
live: Teach at home (Genesis 18:19)
Tonight, read a short passage of Scripture with your children or family and explain it in your own words.
Move your treasure (Luke 12:33)
Set aside what you saved by fasting this week and give it to someone in need.
2027-02-20.prayer: God our Savior, you did not hide your plans from Abraham, and you chose him to teach his household your way. Your goodness and loving kindness appeared in Christ, and you renewed us through the water of rebirth. Make our homes schools of righteousness and justice, free us from fear, and draw our hearts to the treasure of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Father gives the little flock the kingdom, in the Body and Blood of his Son.

2027-02-22.title: Monday of the third week of the Great Fast · The See of St Peter at Antioch
readings: Remember your leaders; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever
2027-02-22.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Feast of the establishment of the Antiochene See of Mar Pathros Sleeha (the Chair of St Peter). The Panchangam also gives John 10:11–18, John 14:1–6 or John 15:9–17 as Gospel. Memorial of Thomas Mar Dioscoros (1943); anniversary of the consecration of St Mary's Cathedral, Thiruvananthapuram (1965).
2027-02-22.verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
theo: Today our Church keeps the feast of the See of St Peter at Antioch. Ancient tradition holds that Peter led the Church at Antioch before he went to Rome, and it was in Antioch “that the disciples were first called ‘Christians.’” Our Syro-Malankara Church, which prays in the Antiochene tradition, honours this throne of the Apostle with special love. It is not a feast of furniture but of a ministry: the Lord said to Peter, “I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.” St Leo the Great taught that the firmness of Peter's faith, which Christ praised, lives on in the Church through his successors (in substance). So the Letter to the Hebrews says: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” Leaders change; the Lord they serve does not.

Genesis shows what a true leader does for his people: he stands before God for them. “Abraham remained standing before the Lord. Then Abraham came near and said, ‘Will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?’” Six times he asks, from fifty righteous down to ten, humbly, “I who am but dust and ashes,” yet boldly: “Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?” And six times God agrees. Intercession is the heart of every shepherd's work. In the Gospel Jesus asks: “Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time?” Peter and his successors, our bishops and priests, are servants who feed the household with the word and the sacraments. Today we also remember Thomas Mar Dioscoros, who died in 1943, and we give thanks for the consecration of St Mary's Cathedral in Thiruvananthapuram in 1965.
outline: Ask: who first spoke the word of God to you?
Feeding the household at the proper time.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Intercede like Abraham (Genesis 18:23)
Choose one town, village or neighbourhood and pray for it by name every day this week.
Remember your leaders (Hebrews 13:7)
Thank God today for the priest or catechist who first taught you the faith, and pray for him or her.
2027-02-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the same yesterday and today and forever. You prayed for Peter that his faith might not fail and made him the rock of your Church, whose throne at Antioch we honour today. Strengthen the Pope, our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and all our bishops in the faith of Peter. Make us intercessors like Abraham and faithful servants in your household. Grant eternal rest to Thomas Mar Dioscoros, and bless all who pray in our cathedral church. Amen.
altar: Through Christ we offer at the altar “a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.”

2027-02-23.title: Tuesday of the third week of the Great Fast · St Polycarp of Smyrna
readings: Lot shelters the angels in Sodom
Come to me, all you that are weary
2027-02-23.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Commemoration of Mar Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna and martyr; name day of Mathews Mar Polycarpos.
2027-02-23.verse: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
theo: Today we remember Mar Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, who as a young man had known St John the Apostle and who was burned for Christ in his old age, about the year 155. The account of his martyrdom, written by his own Church, tells how the proconsul urged him to curse Christ and save his life. Polycarp answered that for eighty-six years he had served Christ and had never been wronged by him: how could he blaspheme the King who had saved him? (in substance). He had carried the yoke of Christ for a lifetime and found it light. Paul explains why: “since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ… we also boast in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit.” Polycarp's hope did not disappoint him.

The first reading is a dark night in Sodom. Lot sits in the gate and, like his uncle Abraham, insists on welcoming the two strangers: “he urged them strongly; so they turned aside to him and entered his house.” Then the men of the city surround the house with violence. Lot's response is itself a terrible wrong: he offers his own daughters to the mob. Scripture records it without approving it; it shows how deeply the sin of a city can twist even a man who wants to do right. It is not Lot who saves the day, but the guests: “the men inside reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.” God's messengers pull him to safety. And Jesus opens another door to all who are crushed by the weight of sin and fear: “Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.” Today we also pray for Mathews Mar Polycarpos on his name day.
outline: Ask: what burden are you carrying into this third week of the Fast?
Point 1 · A dark night in Sodom
The guests reach out and save Lot.
The gentle yoke, the martyr's rest.
“Come to me… and I will give you rest.”
live: Bring your burden (Matthew 11:28)
Write down the heaviest burden you are carrying and leave it before the tabernacle or a holy picture today.
Learn from Polycarp (Romans 5:3–4)
Accept one small hardship today without complaint, offering it for persecuted Christians.
2027-02-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble in heart, you call all who are weary to come to you. You gave Mar Polycarp the strength to serve you faithfully for eighty-six years and to die for you in hope. Pour your love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, so that our sufferings may produce endurance, character and hope. Pull us from every danger as your angels pulled Lot from the night, and give us your rest. Bless Mathews Mar Polycarpos on his name day. Amen.
altar: Polycarp prayed in the fire as one offering a sacrifice (in substance); at the altar we join the one Sacrifice of Christ that gives the martyrs their strength.

2027-02-24.title: Wednesday of the third week of the Great Fast · The Finding of the Head of St John the Baptist
readings: Lot lingers, and the angels take him by the hand
There is no one who is righteous, not even one
The death of John the Baptist
2027-02-24.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Commemoration of the finding of the head of St John the Baptist.
2027-02-24.verse: But he lingered; so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and they brought him out and left him outside the city.
theo: The angels tell Lot to gather his family and leave Sodom, for the city will be destroyed. His sons-in-law think he is joking. At dawn the angels urge him again, “But he lingered.” Lot knows the danger and still cannot bring himself to go; his house, his goods and his habits hold him back.
