Then comes one of the most tender lines in Genesis: “the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and they brought him out.” Even outside he bargains: not the hills, but a little town nearby, “is it not a little one?” And God grants it. In the third week of the Fast many of us are like Lot: we know what we must leave, and we linger. God does not abandon the one who lingers. He takes us by the hand. But he also says: “Flee for your life; do not look back.”

Paul's words are blunt: “There is no one who is righteous, not even one… All have turned aside.” Every mouth is silenced before God, “for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.” No one escapes Sodom by his own goodness; all of us need to be taken by the hand. Today the Church remembers the finding of the head of St John the Baptist, the prophet who called Israel to repentance. The Gospel tells how he died: John had told Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have her,” and for that truth he was imprisoned and beheaded at a banquet, to keep a foolish oath. St John Chrysostom contrasts the two men: John in chains was free, and Herod on his throne was a slave to his passions and to the opinion of his guests (in substance). Herod lingered between conscience and pride and chose pride. John did not linger; he spoke the truth and gave his life. His head, honoured by the Church through the centuries, reminds us that the voice which said “Repent” was not silenced.
outline: Ask: what are you still lingering over in this Fast?
Taken by the hand in mercy.
All need the mercy of God.
live: Stop lingering (Genesis 19:16)
Name one sin or habit you know you must leave, and take one concrete step away from it today.
Speak the truth with love (Matthew 14:4)
Where you have kept silent about something wrong out of fear, ask the Holy Spirit for courage and a gentle word.
2027-02-24.prayer: Merciful Lord, when Lot lingered in Sodom you took him by the hand and led him out. Take us by the hand when we hesitate to leave our sins. We confess that none of us is righteous before you; have mercy on us. Give us the courage of St John the Baptist, who spoke the truth to the powerful and gave his life for it, and keep us free from the pride that enslaved Herod. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Lamb whom John pointed out takes us by the hand at the altar and leads us out of every Sodom of sin.

2027-02-25.title: Thursday of the third week of the Great Fast · Blessed Rani Maria
readings: Lot's wife looks back; God remembered Abraham
Sheep in the midst of wolves
2027-02-25.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Commemoration of Blessed Rani Maria Vattalil, virgin and martyr (killed 25 February 1995).
2027-02-25.verse: But we have this treasure in clay jars, so that it may be made clear that this extraordinary power belongs to God and does not come from us.
theo: Genesis tells the end of Sodom in a few heavy lines: “the Lord rained on Sodom and Gomorrah sulfur and fire from the Lord out of heaven.” Lot reaches Zoar as the sun rises. “But Lot’s wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.” She was already outside the city, already saved, yet her heart had stayed behind. Jesus would later say only three words about her: “Remember Lot’s wife.” Then the reading turns to Abraham, who goes early in the morning to the place where he had pleaded with God and sees the smoke rising. And Scripture adds the reason Lot was spared: “God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow.” Lot was saved because someone had prayed for him. Our intercession for others is never wasted.

Today we remember Blessed Rani Maria Vattalil, a Franciscan Clarist sister born at Pulluvazhy in Kerala, who served the poor in Madhya Pradesh and helped landless families to free themselves from moneylenders. On 25 February 1995 she was stabbed to death on a bus near Indore by a man hired by those who resented her work. Paul's words describe her: “we have this treasure in clay jars… We are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.” Jesus had warned: “I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves.” What followed her death is the fruit of the Gospel: her family forgave the killer; her sister, Sr Selmy Paul, visited him in prison and tied a rakhi on his wrist as a brother; he repented and later came to her beatification at Indore in 2017. Tertullian said that the blood of Christians is seed (in substance). Rani Maria's blood bore the seed of forgiveness.
outline: Ask: what are you tempted to look back at in this Fast?
Saved, but her heart stayed behind.
Rani Maria: struck down, but not destroyed.
“We have this treasure in clay jars.”
live: Do not look back (Genesis 19:26)
Remove one thing from your phone, room or routine that keeps pulling your heart back to an old sin.
Forgive like Rani Maria's family (Matthew 10:22)
Pray today by name for someone who has hurt you or your family, and ask God to bless them.
2027-02-25.prayer: Lord God, you remembered Abraham and rescued Lot from the overthrow. Keep our hearts from looking back to what you have saved us from. You placed the treasure of your Gospel in the clay jar of Blessed Rani Maria and gave her strength to serve the poor and to die for you. Through her prayers, give us courage among wolves, and give our families the grace to forgive as hers forgave. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the altar we receive the treasure of Christ into clay jars, so that the life of Jesus may be made visible in our mortal flesh.

2027-02-26.title: Friday of the third week of the Great Fast
readings: Lot and his daughters in the cave
God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance
Pray to your Father who is in secret
2027-02-26.verse: Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience? Do you not realize that God’s kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?
theo: Today's first reading is one of the saddest pages in Genesis, and Scripture tells it without decoration. Lot, rescued from Sodom, is afraid to stay even in Zoar and goes to live in a cave in the hills with his two daughters. Cut off from everyone, convinced that “there is not a man on earth to come in to us,” the daughters make their father drunk and conceive by him. The sons born are Moab and Ben-ammi, ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites. The Bible does not praise any of this. It shows what happens when fear, isolation and despair take the place of trust in God: a family saved from fire falls into darkness in a cave. Sodom was left behind, but some of Sodom had come along. Yet God's story does not end in the cave. From Moab, many generations later, came Ruth, who said to Naomi, “your people shall be my people, and your God my God,” and who became the great-grandmother of David and an ancestor of Jesus. God can write straight even on the most crooked lines of human history.

Paul warns us not to read such stories with a judging heart: “Therefore you have no excuse, whoever you are, when you judge others; for in passing judgment on another you condemn yourself.” The real question is how I respond to God's patience with me: “Do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience? Do you not realize that God’s kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?” On this Friday Jesus teaches the posture of a repentant heart: not prayer to be seen, but prayer in secret: “go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret.” Nor “empty phrases,” for “your Father knows what you need before you ask him.” St Cyprian wrote that God hears not the voice but the heart, and that the humble prayer of the heart reaches him without words (in substance). Where despair drove Lot's family into a cave, prayer in the secret room opens the soul to the Father who sees.
outline: Ask: what do fear and loneliness lead people to do?
Fear, isolation and sin; yet God brings Ruth from Moab.
The Father who sees in secret.
“God’s kindness is meant to lead you to repentance.”
live: Do not stay in the cave (Genesis 19:30)
If you know someone isolated and afraid, call or visit them this week.
Go into your room (Matthew 6:6)
Find ten minutes alone today, close the door, and pray to the Father without hurry.
2027-02-26.prayer: Merciful Father, you see the darkness into which fear and loneliness can lead us, and you do not abandon us there. Save us from despair, and keep us from judging others when we ourselves need your mercy. Let your kindness lead us to repentance. Teach us to pray to you in secret, with few words and an honest heart, for you know what we need before we ask. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: On this Friday the one who descended into our darkness offers himself for all, Jew and Greek, Moabite and Israelite alike.

2027-02-27.title: Saturday of the third week of the Great Fast
readings: “She is my sister”: God guards Sarah
Doers of the law; conscience bears witness
The Holy Spirit will teach you what to say
2027-02-27.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), third week. Tomorrow is Knanoitho Sunday, the Sunday of the Canaanite woman.
2027-02-27.verse: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart; furthermore it was I who kept you from sinning against me. Therefore I did not let you touch her.
theo: Abraham, the friend of God who had pleaded so boldly for Sodom, now behaves like a frightened man. Living as a foreigner in Gerar, he says of Sarah, “She is my sister,” and King Abimelech takes her. It is a half-truth told out of fear, and it puts at risk the very promise God has just renewed: that Sarah herself will bear Isaac. God steps in, not to Abraham, but to the pagan king in a dream: “You are about to die because of the woman whom you have taken; for she is a married woman.” Abimelech protests his innocence, and God agrees: “Yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart; furthermore it was I who kept you from sinning against me.” Two things stand out. The foreign king has a more honest conscience in this story than the father of believers. And God does not discard his flawed servant: “return the man’s wife; for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you shall live.” God guards his promise even when his friend fails.

Paul says that Abimelech's kind of honesty is no accident: “When Gentiles, who do not possess the law, do instinctively what the law requires… They show that what the law requires is written on their hearts, to which their own conscience also bears witness.” And “it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous in God’s sight, but the doers.” Abraham knew God's word, yet in fear he hid the truth. Jesus asks for the opposite courage: “everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God.” Fear makes us disown what we belong to, as Abraham disowned his wife. But Jesus promises help: “the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.” He also warns that “whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.” St Augustine taught that this sin is the hardness of heart that refuses to the end the forgiveness the Spirit offers (in substance). No one who fears having committed it has committed it; the door of mercy is open to all who knock.
outline: Ask: when did fear make you hide the truth?
The honest conscience of a pagan king.
The Spirit teaches us what to say.
“It was I who kept you from sinning against me.”
live: Tell the whole truth (Genesis 20:2)
Correct today one half-truth you have told out of fear or convenience.
Do not deny whom you belong to (Luke 12:8)
Make the sign of the cross before a meal in public this week, without shame.
2027-02-27.prayer: Lord God, you guarded Sarah and your promise when Abraham failed through fear, and you kept Abimelech from sin. Thank you for the times you have kept us from sinning against you without our knowing. Write your law ever more deeply on our hearts, make us doers of your word, and give us courage to acknowledge your Son before others. Holy Spirit, teach us what to say. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Lord who keeps us from sin and forgives our failures feeds us at the altar, so that we may confess him before others.

quick: The Lord enters his Temple in Mary's arms.
Simeon: “My eyes have seen your salvation.”
Joy and the sword: the Child will give himself for us.
2027-02-02.action: Present your day to God each morning this week.
2027-02-02.question: Have I presented my life, my family and my work to God?

illus: An illustration

family.ask: Ask: “How can we offer our family to God this week?”

kidsaint: Two very old people who prayed in the Temple every day, waiting for the Saviour. God let them see baby Jesus before they died. Lesson: keep praying and waiting for God; he keeps his promises.
term: Syriac for “entrance”: the feast of the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple, 2 February, forty days after Yaldo. In the West it is called the Presentation of the Lord.
termMore: Luke 2:29–32, “Now, Lord, let your servant go in peace”, is prayed in many Christian traditions at night prayer, at the end of the day.

quick: Our Lent begins at a wedding: the Fast is transformation, not sadness.
Mary's advice for Lent: “Do whatever he tells you.”
The fast God chooses: return with the heart, share with the poor.
2027-02-07.action: Make a family Lenten plan: one fast, one prayer, one work of charity.
2027-02-07.question: What water in my life do I want Jesus to change into wine this Lent?
2027-02-07.special: Kothine Sunday, first Sunday of the Great Fast. The special prayers of Lent begin this evening; remind the faithful about fasting and abstinence and about Shubkono on Monday.
illus: An illustration

In many Malankara homes the meat pots are scrubbed clean on the evening before the Fast, and the family begins fifty days of simpler food. The clean pots are like the jars at Cana: emptied and ready to be filled with something better.

family.explain: At a wedding in Cana the wine ran out. Mary told the servants: “Do whatever Jesus tells you.” Jesus changed water into the best wine! In Lent Jesus wants to change our hearts too.
family.intention: We pray for a holy Lent for our family, and for people who have no food.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give up this Lent, and what good thing will we do?”

kidsaint: His name means “son of encouragement”. In Antioch he encouraged the new Christians, and brought Paul to teach with him; there the disciples were first called Christians. Lesson: encourage others to be good this Lent.
term: Kothine refers to the wedding at Cana (John 2:1–11). The Malankara Church begins the Great Fast with this Gospel: the Fast is a time of transformation, from water to wine.
termMore: The service of forgiveness (reconciliation) on the first Monday of the Fast. Priest and people ask forgiveness of one another and of God before beginning the fifty days.

quick: Lent is a season of healing: Christ the physician.
Jesus touches the untouchable and makes him clean.
Healing needs humility: kneel like the leper, wash like Naaman.
2027-02-14.action: Make a good Confession during this week of the Fast.
2027-02-14.question: What “leprosy” in my life am I hiding from Jesus?
2027-02-14.special: Garbo Sunday, second Sunday of the Great Fast.
illus: An illustration

Kerala once had leprosy hospitals run by religious sisters, who washed and bandaged patients whom even their families had abandoned. Visitors were amazed that the sisters touched them with bare hands. They had learnt it from Jesus.

family.explain: A man with a skin disease called leprosy was alone; nobody would touch him. He asked Jesus for help, and Jesus touched him and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for the sick, and for people who are left alone or rejected.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is lonely at school or at work, and how can we be kind to them?”

kidsaint: A Belgian priest who went to live with people suffering from leprosy on the island of Molokai, cared for them, built homes and a church, and finally caught the disease himself. Lesson: love the people others avoid.
term: Garbo is Syriac for “leper”. The second Sunday of the Great Fast, when the Church reads the healing of the leper. The Sundays of the Fast are named after Christ's healings.
termMore: The Malankara Great Fast follows Christ the physician from Sunday to Sunday: the leper, the paralytic, the Canaanite woman's daughter, the bent woman and the man born blind. Lent is our journey of healing towards Easter.

quick: Four friends carry the paralytic to Jesus: we carry each other by faith.
Jesus heals the deepest paralysis first: sin.
Don't only hear the Word; do it.
2027-02-21.action: Pray daily this week for one person who is far from God.
2027-02-21.question: Whom am I carrying to Jesus, and who is carrying me?
2027-02-21.special: M'shario Sunday, third Sunday of the Great Fast.
illus: An illustration

When a young man in a Kerala parish was bedridden after an accident, his prayer group came every Friday evening, carried him to the car and took him to the adoration chapel. He says their faith kept his alive. They were the four friends of Capernaum.

family.explain: Four friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. The house was full, so they made a hole in the roof! Jesus forgave his sins and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot walk or are sick in bed, and for friends who are far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we help a friend to come closer to Jesus?”

kidsaint: A Franciscan Clarist sister from Pulluvazhy in Kerala who worked for poor village families in Madhya Pradesh and was killed in 1995. Her killer later repented, and her family forgave him. Lesson: love and forgiveness can heal hearts.
term: M'shario refers to the paralytic, the man who was “loosed” and raised up. The third Sunday of the Great Fast reads his healing (Mark 2:1–12).
termMore: On the weekdays of the Great Fast the Malankara tradition prays with prostrations (kneeling and bowing to the ground), a bodily sign of repentance. They are not made on the Fortieth Friday and on feast days, as the lectionary notes.

quick: Persevering prayer: when God seems silent, keep asking.
Humble faith wins mercy: “even the dogs eat the crumbs.”
God's house is a house of prayer for all peoples.
2027-02-28.action: Take up again a prayer you stopped because God seemed silent.
2027-02-28.question: Have I given up asking God for something important?
2027-02-28.special: Knanoitho Sunday, fourth Sunday of the Great Fast. Announce the middle day of the Fast (Wednesday 3 March) and the erection of the Cross.
illus: An illustration

A Kerala mother prayed for twenty years for her son who had left home and faith. Every Sunday she lit a candle before Mary. When he came back one Easter, he said: “I knew someone was praying.” The Canaanite woman still lives in our parishes.

family.explain: A mother whose daughter was very sick kept asking Jesus for help, even when he did not answer at first. Because she kept trusting, Jesus healed her daughter.
family.intention: We pray for all mothers and fathers who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we need to keep asking Jesus for as a family?”

kidsaint: Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold as a slave, she later came to know Jesus in Italy, became a sister, and forgave those who had hurt her. Lesson: God's love is for everyone, from every nation.
term: Knanoitho means “the Canaanite woman”. The fourth Sunday of the Great Fast reads the healing of her daughter (Matthew 15:21–28; Mark 7:24–30).
termMore: On the Wednesday after this Sunday, the twenty-fifth day of the Fast, the Malankara Church marks the middle of the Great Fast; the Cross (Gogultho) is solemnly set up in the church, recalling the bronze serpent lifted up in the desert (Numbers 21:9; John 3:14).

quick: Paul prays that we may know God's will and live worthy of the Lord.
God has moved us from darkness into the kingdom of his Son.
Jesus teaches us to ask forgiveness as we forgive.
2027-02-01.action: Say one Our Father slowly today and pray for someone you need to forgive.
2027-02-01.question: Is there anyone whose name makes the line “as we forgive” hard for me to say?

family.explain: Jesus taught us his own prayer. We call God “our Father”, so we are all brothers and sisters. In the prayer we ask God to forgive us, and we promise to forgive others too.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is sad or hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to say sorry to, or forgive, this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Mavelikara taught her grandchildren the Our Father in Malayalam and in Syriac. One evening the boy stopped in the middle and refused to go on. His sister had broken his toy, he said, and he could not say ‘as we forgive’. The grandmother waited quietly. After a minute he went to his sister, shook her hand, came back and finished the prayer. She told him: now you have really prayed it.

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Teach us to pray. Amen.
share: Filled with the knowledge of God's will (Colossians 1:9). What do I ask for when I pray for others?
He has rescued us from the power of darkness (Colossians 1:13). Where have I seen his light this year?
As we also have forgiven our debtors (Matthew 6:12). Whom do I still need to forgive?
pm.resp: Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For our parish as it prepares for the Great Fast.
For families divided by quarrels over property or words.
For those who find it hard to forgive.
For those we have hurt.
For the sick and the dying, and for the departed faithful we remembered on Sunday.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to call you ours. Make us one family that forgives, and lead us into the Fast with clean hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Simeon waited for the consolation of Israel and was guided by the Spirit.
Anna prayed and fasted night and day, then spoke about the child to all.
Paul prays that Christ may dwell in our hearts through faith.
2027-02-03.action: Call or visit an elderly person and ask for their prayers.
2027-02-03.question: Has my waiting on God made me bitter or ready?

family.explain: Anna was a very old lady who lived in the temple and prayed all the time. When she saw baby Jesus, she was so happy that she told everyone about him!
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all the old people we know.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to make an old person happy?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kottarakkara an old widow came to the church every morning at six, for more than thirty years, and sat in the same corner with her rosary. When she died, the vicar found a worn notebook in her bag. On every page were names: priests, young couples, sick children, boys abroad looking for work. Many in the parish discovered that day that she had been praying for them by name for years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Simeon and Anna waited for you and saw you. Open our eyes to see you today. Amen.
share: Guided by the Spirit, Simeon came into the temple (Luke 2:27). Do I let the Spirit lead my steps?
She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer (Luke 2:37). What will my prayer look like in the Fast?
Rooted and grounded in love (Ephesians 3:17). What are my roots?
pm.resp: Lord, let us see your salvation.
interc: For grandparents and the elderly, especially those who live alone.
For widows and widowers.
For those who have waited long for an answer to prayer.
For our parish elders who pray for us unseen.
For all who will begin the Great Fast next week.
pm.close: Father, you rewarded the long waiting of Simeon and Anna with the sight of your Son. Keep us faithful in prayer until we too see him face to face. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul calls himself a debtor to everyone, wise and simple.
He is not ashamed of the gospel, the power of God for salvation.
St John de Britto lived as a poor Tamil ascetic and died a martyr at Oriyur.
2027-02-04.action: Share one word of faith today with someone who does not know Christ well.
2027-02-04.question: Where am I ashamed of the gospel?

family.explain: St John de Britto came all the way from Portugal to Tamil Nadu. He dressed and ate like the poor people there and told them about Jesus. He was not ashamed of Jesus, even when it cost him his life.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries in India and all over the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a place where we feel shy to pray or to say we are Christians?”

illus: An illustration

A software engineer from Thiruvalla was sharing a hostel room in Chennai with three colleagues. On the first night he hesitated, then knelt by his bed and made the sign of the cross. Nobody laughed. A week later one of the others asked him, quietly, what he prayed about. That began a friendship that lasted years. He said later: the hardest part was the first ten seconds on my knees.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us the courage of your martyrs and make us unashamed of your gospel. Amen.
share: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians (Romans 1:14). To whom do I owe the gospel?
I am not ashamed of the gospel (Romans 1:16). When have I hidden my faith?
The gate is narrow and the road is hard (Matthew 7:14). What easy road am I tempted to take?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bold for your gospel.
interc: For the Church in Tamil Nadu and for the shrine at Oriyur.
For missionaries and catechists in North and South India.
For Christians who are mocked or threatened for their faith.
For students and workers living far from home.
For courage in our own families to pray openly.
pm.close: Father, St John de Britto followed your Son through the narrow gate to martyrdom. Give us his love and his courage, and bring us all to the life that has no end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Israel had all God's gifts and still fell in the wilderness.
God is faithful and will not let us be tested beyond our strength.
The world that hated Jesus will also hate his disciples.
2027-02-05.action: Pray today for Christians who are persecuted for their faith.
2027-02-05.question: Do I think I am standing so firmly that I no longer watch?

family.explain: Sometimes it is hard to be good. Paul says God is faithful: he never gives us a test that is too big for us, and he always shows us a way out.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are hurt or chased away because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing that often makes me do wrong, and how can we help each other avoid it?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from Pathanamthitta working in a Gulf city told his parish group how he had nearly given up praying. His roommates mocked him and his manager scheduled work on Sundays. One night, ready to stop, he found a small Malankara community meeting in a flat two streets away. They prayed the evening Ramsho in Malayalam. He said: God did not take the test away, but he showed me the door out of loneliness.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are faithful. Keep us standing in the time of testing. Amen.
share: The rock was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). Where do I drink from each day?
So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall (1 Corinthians 10:12). Where am I overconfident?
If they persecuted me, they will persecute you (John 15:20). How do I respond when I am mocked for my faith?
pm.resp: Lord, be our strength in testing.
interc: For Christians persecuted in India and in other lands.
For those tempted to give up their faith.
For young people living far from home and Church.
For all who struggle with addictions.
For our parish as the Great Fast draws near.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful and never let us be tested beyond our strength. Hold us fast in the hour of trial and bring us safely through it. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The rich fool planned only for himself and forgot God.
Paul tells the rich to hope in God and be generous.
Fasting and almsgiving go together.
2027-02-06.action: Set aside money for the poor for the whole Great Fast.
2027-02-06.question: Whom does my barn have room for?

family.explain: A rich man had so much grain that he built bigger barns, but he never thought of God or of hungry people. Jesus says the real treasure is being rich toward God, sharing with others.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough food today.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share during the Great Fast, as a family?”

illus: An illustration

A rubber planter near Ranni kept a small box beside the family altar. Every Lent each member of the family put into it whatever they saved by fasting: the price of a meal, a film, a new shirt. On Pesaha they opened it together and decided whom to help. One year it paid a poor neighbour's daughter's school fees. The children remembered that box long after they forgot the food they had given up.

pm.open: Lord, you give us all good things. Make us rich toward you. Amen.
share: Not to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches (1 Timothy 6:17). Where is my security?
Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years (Luke 12:19). What am I storing up?
Rich in good works, generous, and ready to share (1 Timothy 6:18). What will I give in the Fast?
pm.resp: Lord, make us rich toward you.
interc: For the poor and hungry in our town.
For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and the Catholicos Day collection.
For farmers and all who work the land.
For those who trust in money more than in God.
For the grace of a good Great Fast for our parish.
pm.close: Father, all we have comes from your hand. Teach us to share it with joy, so that we may be rich toward you and take hold of true life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abram believed God's promise and was reckoned righteous.
The Fast opens with Shubkono: we forgive one another as God forgave us.
Jesus fasted forty days and lived by every word of God.
2027-02-08.action: Ask forgiveness of one person today, or offer it, before sunset.
2027-02-08.question: With whom must I make peace for my fast to please God?

family.explain: Today the Great Fast begins. Before we give up food, our Church asks us to say sorry and forgive one another. That is why we hug and ask pardon at Shubkono.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that we may live these forty days in peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family I need to say sorry to today?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Adoor two brothers had not spoken for six years over a boundary wall. At Shubkono, when the people moved forward to ask pardon of one another, the younger brother found himself face to face with the elder. For a moment neither moved. Then the elder bowed and said: forgive me. They walked home together. The wall is still there, but now there is a gate in it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, as we begin the Great Fast, forgive us and teach us to forgive. Amen.
share: He believed the Lord (Genesis 15:6). What promise of God do I find hard to believe?
Do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:26). Whom do I need to forgive today?
One does not live by bread alone (Matthew 4:4). How will I feed on God's word in this Fast?
pm.resp: Lord, make us forgiving as you have forgiven us.
interc: For our parish, that the Fast may be a time of reconciliation.
For broken families and divided brothers and sisters.
For those who fast because they have no food.
For those who are tempted and feel alone.
For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, bishops and priests as they lead us through the Fast.
pm.close: Father, your Son fasted for us in the wilderness. Make these forty days a time of faith, forgiveness and new life, and bring us rejoicing to the feast of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abram offered a sacrifice and drove away the birds of prey.
There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
Jesus is the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep.
2027-02-09.action: Drive away one distraction from your prayer today.
2027-02-09.question: What birds of prey come down on my fast?

family.explain: A good shepherd knows each of his sheep by name and protects them from the wolf. Jesus is our Good Shepherd. He knows each of us and gave his life for us.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, who are shepherds in Jesus' name.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we listen better to Jesus' voice during the Fast?”

illus: An illustration

A goatherd in the hills near Idukki was asked by a visiting boy how he could tell his forty goats apart. He laughed and called one name. A small brown goat lifted its head and came running. He said: I have named every one. When the rain is heavy I carry the weak ones on my shoulders. They know my voice because they know I will not leave them.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, we are your sheep. Let us hear your voice. Amen.
share: How am I to know? (Genesis 15:8). What question do I bring to God in this Fast?
To set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace (Romans 8:6). What fills my mind most of the day?
I know my own and my own know me (John 10:14). Do I know the Shepherd's voice?
pm.resp: Good Shepherd, hold us close.
interc: For our bishops and priests, shepherds of the flock.
For those who have wandered from the Church.
For Christians separated from one another, that there may be one flock.
For those who feel condemned and without hope.
For all who are keeping the Fast with difficulty.
pm.close: Father, your Son laid down his life for his sheep. Keep us in his flock, free from condemnation and alive in the Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God alone passed between the pieces: his covenant rests on his faithfulness.
Paul presses on toward the goal, forgetting what lies behind.
Peter confesses Jesus as the Messiah of God; our Church gives thanks for its Major Archiepiscopal status (2005).
2027-02-10.action: Pray today for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and the Holy Synod.
2027-02-10.question: Who do I say that Jesus is, not in words but in my choices?

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do you say I am? Peter said: you are the Messiah, the Christ of God. Our Church today thanks God that it is one family with Peter's successor, the Pope.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and for all our bishops.
family.ask: Ask: “If Jesus asked me, ‘Who am I for you?’, what would I say?”

illus: An illustration

An old catechism teacher in Thiruvananthapuram kept two photographs above her desk: one of Mar Ivanios, who led the reunion of 1930, and one of the crowd at Pattom on the day the Major Archiepiscopal Church was celebrated in 2005. She told her students: the first man walked a hard road so that we could stand in that crowd. Your road will also be hard. Keep walking.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the Messiah of God. Make us confess you with our lips and our lives. Amen.
share: A flaming torch passed between these pieces (Genesis 15:17). Where have I seen God's faithfulness in my life?
Forgetting what lies behind (Philippians 3:13). What past do I need to let go?
But who do you say that I am? (Luke 9:20). What is my answer today?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us faithful to you.
interc: For Pope Leo and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos.
For the Holy Synod and all the eparchies of our Church in India and abroad.
For the unity of all the Churches of the Malankara tradition.
For our priests and religious, that they may press on toward the goal.
For our parish as we keep the first week of the Great Fast.
pm.close: Father, you have been faithful to our Church through all its history. Keep us one in the faith of Peter, pressing on toward the heavenly call in Christ Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sarai's plan made without God broke her household and hurt Hagar.
Our life is hidden with Christ in God; we seek the things above.
Mary sings that God lifts up the lowly; at Lourdes she came to a poor sick girl.
2027-02-11.action: Visit, call or pray by name for a sick person today.
2027-02-11.question: Where am I forcing my own plan instead of waiting on God?

family.explain: Mary sang a happy song because God loves the small and humble. At Lourdes, Mary appeared to a poor girl named Bernadette, and many sick people still go there to pray.
family.intention: We pray for all the sick people we know, by name.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we cheer up this week: a sick relative, a neighbour, an old friend?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Changanassery working in a cancer ward abroad keeps a small bottle of Lourdes water in her pocket. She does not push it on anyone. But some nights, when a patient cannot sleep from fear, she asks quietly if they would like her to pray. Many say yes. She says the Magnificat in a whisper. She told her parish: I cannot cure them, but I can remind them that God looks with favour on the lowly.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, with you we magnify the Lord. Pray for us and for all the sick. Amen.
share: It may be that I shall obtain children by her (Genesis 16:2). When have I run ahead of God?
Your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). What does it mean for me to be hidden?
He has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant (Luke 1:48). Do I believe God sees my lowliness?
pm.resp: Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the sick, especially those in hospital today.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick.
For pilgrims to Lourdes and to our Marian shrines in Kerala.
For women who are treated harshly and run away from home.
For our parish, that we may keep the Fast in humility.
pm.close: Father, you looked with favour on the lowliness of Mary. Through her prayers, comfort the sick, lift up the lowly, and make us humble servants of your will. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The angel of the Lord found Hagar in the wilderness; she named God “the God who sees.”
God's law is written on human hearts; conscience bears witness.
Jesus promises to acknowledge those who acknowledge him before others.
2027-02-12.action: Make an honest examination of conscience tonight.
2027-02-12.question: Where have I come from, and where am I going?

family.explain: Hagar was alone and frightened in the desert. But God found her and spoke to her. She called God “the God who sees me.” God sees each of us too, always, and he cares.
family.intention: We pray for people who are lonely, runaways and refugees.
family.ask: Ask: “When did I feel that God saw me and helped me?”

illus: An illustration

A social worker in Kottayam who runs a shelter for women says the first words she hears from most newcomers are: no one knew what was happening to me. She keeps a small sign in Malayalam above the door of the shelter: the God who sees me. One woman told her later: when I read that, I cried for the first time in years. I realised someone had been watching over me all along.

pm.open: God who sees, look upon us in our wilderness and lead us home. Amen.
share: Where have you come from and where are you going? (Genesis 16:8). How would I answer?
Written on their hearts (Romans 2:15). What is my conscience telling me in this Fast?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Luke 12:8). Where do I hesitate to acknowledge Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, you see us; have mercy on us.
interc: For runaways, refugees and migrants.
For women and children who suffer harsh treatment at home.
For those who follow their conscience without knowing Christ.
For Christians brought before courts and authorities because of their faith.
For all who will make a confession during this Fast.
pm.close: Father, you saw Hagar in the wilderness and heard her affliction. See every suffering person today, and through the Cross of your Son bring them home. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God called Abram to walk before him and gave him a new name, Abraham.
God's word is living and active and judges the heart.
The wise build on rock by doing what they hear; Ephrem, Theodore and Haggai did.
2027-02-13.action: Pray the Prayer of St Ephrem today with a bow at each line.
2027-02-13.question: Do I only say “Lord, Lord”, or do I do the Father's will?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about two houses. One was built on rock and stood strong in the storm. One was built on sand and fell down. When we listen to Jesus and do what he says, our life is strong like the house on the rock.
family.intention: We pray that our family may listen to Jesus and obey him.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asks us to do that we can do this week?”

illus: An illustration

After the 2018 floods a mason in Chengannur was asked to rebuild a house that had collapsed. He dug far deeper than the family thought necessary, down past the soft soil. They complained of the cost. He said: the old house looked fine for forty years; it fell in one night. I will not build you another beautiful house on mud. In the next heavy monsoon, theirs was one of the few houses on the street that did not crack.

pm.open: Lord, your word is living and active. Let it build our lives on rock. Amen.
share: Walk before me, and be blameless (Genesis 17:1). What does walking before God mean for me this week?
The word of God is living and active (Hebrews 4:12). Which word of Scripture has pierced me in this first week?
Hears these words of mine and acts on them (Matthew 7:24). What have I heard but not yet done?
pm.resp: Lord, make us doers of your word.
interc: For our parish as we complete the first week of the Fast.
For all who teach the faith, as Mar Aprem did, especially Sunday-school teachers and choirs.
For soldiers and all who serve in the armed forces.
For those rebuilding their homes and lives after disaster.
For Christians who suffer for refusing to deny Christ.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to build on the rock of his word. Through the prayers of Mar Aprem, Mar Theodore and the Prophet Haggai, make us hearers and doers of that word throughout this Fast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God gave Abraham circumcision as the sign of his covenant.
Paul asks for steady prayer and speech seasoned with salt.
Jesus says: do not worry; strive first for the kingdom of God.
2027-02-15.action: Before any harsh word today, pause and choose a gracious one.
2027-02-15.question: What worry do I carry that the Father already knows about?

family.explain: Jesus told us to look at the birds and the flowers. Birds do not have kitchens or shops, but God feeds them. Flowers do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. If God cares for them, he cares for us much more.
family.intention: We pray for families who are worried about food, money or work.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one worry we can give to God together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A fish seller in Neendakara used to wake at three every morning with her stomach knotted: would the boats come in, would the price be fair, would there be enough for school fees? One Lent her parish priest suggested she say one sentence before she left the house: Father, you know what we need today. She said it grudgingly at first. The boats did not come in more often. But she noticed that she stopped snapping at her children over breakfast, and that she had begun to sing on the way to the harbour.

pm.open: Father in heaven, you know what we need before we ask. Take our worries and give us your kingdom. Amen.
share: So shall my covenant be in your flesh (Genesis 17:13). What in my daily life shows that I belong to God?
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt (Colossians 4:6). How did my words taste to others this past week?
Do not worry about tomorrow (Matthew 6:34). What tomorrow am I carrying today?
pm.resp: Father, we seek first your kingdom.
interc: For Mathews Mar Pachomios on the anniversary of his ordination, and for all our bishops.
For those who are anxious about money, food or work.
For fishermen, farmers and all who depend on weather and harvest.
For those whose words have wounded others, and for those they wounded.
For catechumens and all preparing for baptism this Easter.
pm.close: Father, you feed the birds and clothe the lilies. Free us from anxiety, season our speech with grace, and keep us faithful to the covenant sealed in the blood of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God renamed Sarai as Sarah and promised Abraham a son, Isaac.
We are saved by grace through faith, for the good works God prepared.
Jesus says: you will know them by their fruits.
2027-02-16.action: Thank God tonight for three gifts you did not earn.
2027-02-16.question: What fruit does my life bear when no one is watching?

family.explain: Grace means a gift we did not earn. Our life, our family, our baptism: all are gifts from God. God gives us his love first, and then helps us do good works, like a tree that grows fruit.
family.intention: We pray that our family may bear good fruit: kindness, patience and joy.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit do we see in each other?”

illus: An illustration

A retired headmaster in Punalur planted a jackfruit tree when his first grandchild was born. For years it gave only leaves, and his neighbours told him to cut it down. He watered it, manured it and waited. In the eighth year it gave so much fruit that he sent jackfruit to every house on the lane. When people thanked him he would point at the tree and say: do not thank me. I only waited. It did what it was made to do.

pm.open: God rich in mercy, we are alive only by your grace. Make us bear fruit for you. Amen.
share: Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? (Genesis 17:17). What promise of God seems too good to be true for me?
By grace you have been saved through faith (Ephesians 2:8). Do I still try to earn God's love?
You will know them by their fruits (Matthew 7:16). What fruit would others say my life bears?
pm.resp: Lord, by your grace make us fruitful.
interc: For couples who long for a child.
For those who feel spiritually dead and far from God.
For preachers and teachers, that they may be true prophets known by good fruit.
For children and young people growing in faith.
For those whose prayers seem unanswered.
pm.close: Father, you are rich in mercy and you made us alive with your Son. Keep us rooted in your grace, so that our lives may bear the good fruit you prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham obeyed God “that very day.”
In Christ are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
Jesus asks us to follow him without delay or excuse.
2027-02-17.action: Do today one good thing you have been postponing.
2027-02-17.question: What do I put first before following Jesus?

family.explain: Some people wanted to follow Jesus, but said: later, not now. Jesus said: follow me now. Abraham also obeyed God the same day he heard him. When God asks something good of us, the best time is today.
family.intention: We pray that our family may not delay in doing good.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing have we been saying we will do later?”

illus: An illustration

A young mother in Kattappana kept a list on the fridge of people she meant to visit: an aunt in hospital, a friend who had lost her husband, a neighbour who had moved away. Every week the list grew. One Lent she decided to cross off one name each week, whatever happened. In the third week she visited the aunt in hospital, who held her hand for an hour and told her stories of her own mother. The aunt died the following Tuesday. The young woman still keeps the list, but now it is short.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we want to follow you. Take away our delays and our excuses. Amen.
share: That very day Abraham obeyed (Genesis 17:26). What have I been postponing that God asked of me?
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:3). Do I treat Christ as my greatest treasure?
Lord, first let me go (Matthew 8:21). What do I put first?
pm.resp: Lord, we will follow you.
interc: For those who are discerning a call to priesthood or religious life.
For the homeless and all who have nowhere to lay their heads.
For those who keep postponing their return to God.
For families grieving the death of a parent.
For unity and love among the members of our parish.
pm.close: Father, your Son had nowhere to lay his head, yet he is our treasure. Give us hearts that obey without delay and follow him wherever he goes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham ran to welcome three guests at Mamre and served them a feast.
We are the temple of the living God, who walks among us.
The king invites all to the wedding banquet, but asks for the wedding robe.
2027-02-18.action: Invite or visit someone who is alone this week.
2027-02-18.question: Do I come to the Lord's table clothed in love?

family.explain: Three visitors came to Abraham's tent on a hot day. Abraham ran to welcome them, washed their feet and made them a big meal. Later he found out that God had visited him! When we welcome guests kindly, we welcome God.
family.intention: We pray for guests, strangers and those who have no one to visit them.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make guests feel welcome in our home?”

illus: An illustration

In a small house near Pathanapuram an old couple kept a custom from their parents: whoever knocked at mealtime was given a plate before anyone in the family ate. Their children found it embarrassing; sometimes it was a beggar, sometimes a salesman, once a lost tourist. When the old man died, a stranger stood at the back of the funeral and wept. Afterwards he told the family: twenty years ago I came to your door with nothing. Your father fed me first. I have never forgotten that I was served before his own children.

pm.open: Lord, you came as a guest to Abraham. Come and dwell in us, your temple. Amen.
share: He ran from the tent entrance to meet them (Genesis 18:2). Do I run to welcome others, or wait to see if they are worth it?
We are the temple of the living God (2 Corinthians 6:16). What idol needs to be removed from my temple?
Friend, how did you get in here without a wedding robe? (Matthew 22:12). What would the King find lacking in me?
pm.resp: Lord, clothe us in love.
interc: For migrants, strangers and travellers far from home.
For families who practise hospitality, especially to the poor.
For those who have made light of God's invitation.
For the Church, that she may be a house open to all.
For those preparing to receive the Holy Qurbono for the first time.
pm.close: Father, you invite all people to the wedding banquet of your Son. Make us welcoming like Abraham, holy as your temple, and clothed in the charity that befits your feast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sarah laughed in disbelief, but God asked: is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
Paul counts everything as loss for the surpassing value of knowing Christ.
Jesus says: no one will snatch my sheep out of my hand.
2027-02-19.action: Spend some time today before a crucifix.
2027-02-19.question: Where have I quietly stopped believing that God can act?

family.explain: Sarah heard that she would have a baby when she was very old, and she laughed because she thought it was impossible. But God said: is anything too wonderful for the Lord? And the baby was born. God can do things we think are impossible.
family.intention: We pray for people who have lost hope.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we think is impossible that we can ask God for?”

illus: An illustration

A widow in Nedumangad prayed for twenty-two years for her son, who had left the faith and stopped speaking to the family. Her friends stopped asking about him; she once admitted she had begun to pray for him the way one waters a dead plant, out of habit. One Good Friday he appeared at the back of the church during the veneration of the cross. Afterwards he said only: I was passing by and heard the singing. She told the priest later: I am ashamed. I had stopped expecting anything. God had not stopped.

pm.open: Lord, nothing is too wonderful for you. Revive our hope. Amen.
share: Sarah laughed to herself (Genesis 18:12). What hidden disbelief do I carry?
The surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord (Philippians 3:8). What do I value more than knowing Christ?
No one will snatch them out of my hand (John 10:28). When have I felt held by Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, hold us in your hand.
interc: For Joseph Mar Thomas on the anniversary of his ordination, and for all bishops.
For mothers and fathers praying for children who have left the faith.
For those who have stopped hoping.
For Christians who have lost everything for Christ's sake.
For the dying, that they may rest in the Father's hand.
pm.close: Father, nothing is too wonderful for you, and no one can snatch us from your hand. On this Friday, unite us to the sufferings of your Son and give us the power of his resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God chose Abraham to teach his household to do righteousness and justice.
God saved us by his mercy, through the water of rebirth and the Holy Spirit.
Jesus says: do not be afraid, little flock; where your treasure is, there your heart will be.
2027-02-20.action: Give away today what you saved by fasting this week.
2027-02-20.question: Where is my treasure, and so where is my heart?

family.explain: Jesus calls us his little flock and says: do not be afraid. God wants to give us his kingdom. He asks us to share what we have with the poor, because what we give in love is kept safe in heaven.
family.intention: We pray for poor families, and for our family to be generous.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share this week with someone who has less?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolboy in Kundara asked his grandfather why the family always ate a plain supper on Saturdays in Lent. The old man took him to a small tin behind the holy pictures. Inside were coins and folded notes, the money saved each week. On Holy Thursday they would take it to an old couple down the road who had no children. The boy asked: why not just give it now? His grandfather said: because every Saturday, when you are hungry, you will remember them. That is how a heart learns where its treasure is.

pm.open: Father, you are pleased to give us the kingdom. Free us from fear and draw our hearts to you. Amen.
share: That he may charge his children and his household (Genesis 18:19). What am I handing on to the next generation?
He saved us... according to his mercy (Titus 3:5). How have I experienced God's mercy this week?
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Luke 12:34). Where is my heart?
pm.resp: Father, be our treasure.
interc: For parents and grandparents who hand on the faith at home.
For the victims of injustice whose cry rises to God.
For catechumens preparing for the water of rebirth this Easter.
For the poor who will receive the alms of this Fast.
For our parish as we approach M'shario Sunday.
pm.close: Father, it is your good pleasure to give us the kingdom. Make our homes places of faith, our hearts free from fear, and our hands open to the poor. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham stood before the Lord and pleaded for the righteous in Sodom.
Remember your leaders and imitate their faith; Jesus Christ is the same forever.
The faithful servant feeds the household at the proper time.
2027-02-22.action: Pray today for the Pope and for your bishop by name.
2027-02-22.question: For whom do I stand before God as Abraham did?

family.explain: Abraham asked God to save a city if even a few good people lived there. He kept asking, again and again, and God listened. Today we remember St Peter, whom Jesus made the leader of his apostles. We pray for our Church's leaders, as Abraham prayed for others.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope, our Catholicos and our bishop.
family.ask: Ask: “Which place or person shall we pray for, like Abraham?”

illus: An illustration

A retired bus conductor in Neyyattinkara spends his mornings on a bench outside the parish church with a small notebook. In it are the names of the streets on his old route. Each day he prays for one street, from the first stop to the last, and then starts again. When people ask him why, he says: for thirty years I took these people where they needed to go. Now I can only take them to God. Some days he adds a name someone has whispered to him on the bench.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the same yesterday, today and forever. Strengthen your Church in the faith of Peter. Amen.
share: Abraham remained standing before the Lord (Genesis 18:22). For whom am I willing to plead before God?
Remember your leaders... imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Whose faith do I want to imitate?
Who then is the faithful and wise slave? (Matthew 24:45). Am I faithful in what is entrusted to me?
pm.resp: Lord, keep your Church firm in faith.
interc: For the Pope, successor of Peter, and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos.
For our bishops and priests, faithful servants of the household.
For cities and villages where evil seems stronger than good.
For the soul of Thomas Mar Dioscoros and all departed shepherds of our Church.
For all who worship in St Mary's Cathedral, Thiruvananthapuram, and in every parish of our Church.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the faith of Peter. Through his prayers keep us united, make us bold intercessors like Abraham, and let us be found faithful when your Son returns. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Lot sheltered God's messengers, and they pulled him to safety from the violent crowd.
Suffering produces endurance, character and hope, and hope does not disappoint us.
Jesus invites all who are weary to come to him and find rest.
2027-02-23.action: Offer one hardship today for persecuted Christians.
2027-02-23.question: What heavy burden do I need to bring to Jesus?

family.explain: Jesus says: come to me, all who are tired and carrying heavy things, and I will give you rest. Today we remember St Polycarp, an old bishop who loved Jesus all his life. When he was told to say bad things about Jesus, he said: Jesus has always been good to me; how can I speak against him?
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “What is heavy in our hearts that we can give to Jesus tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A porter at a railway station in Kollam carried other people's luggage for forty years. His back was bent and his knees were bad. When his grandson asked if he was ever tired, he laughed and said: always. But every morning before work he stopped at the church near the station for two minutes. What do you do there? the boy asked. He said: I put down my own load first. Then I can carry other people's.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we are weary and burdened. We come to you for rest. Amen.
share: The men inside reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house (Genesis 19:10). When has God pulled me back from danger?
Suffering produces endurance (Romans 5:3). How has a past suffering shaped my character?
I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:29). What do I need to learn from Jesus' gentleness?
pm.resp: Lord, give us your rest.
interc: For Mathews Mar Polycarpos on his name day, and for all our bishops.
For Christians persecuted for their faith.
For the elderly who have served the Lord for many years.
For those caught in cities and places of violence.
For all who are weary and burdened.
pm.close: Father, you strengthened Mar Polycarp to bear witness to your Son in old age and in fire. Pour your love into our hearts, give us hope that does not disappoint, and lead us to the rest of Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Lot lingered in Sodom, but the angels took him by the hand in God's mercy.
No one is righteous on his own; all need God's mercy.
John the Baptist spoke the truth to Herod and gave his life for it.
2027-02-24.action: Take one concrete step away from a sin you have been lingering over.
2027-02-24.question: What keeps me lingering when God says: flee?

family.explain: God sent angels to save Lot and his family from a bad city. Lot was slow and did not want to go. So the angels took them by the hand and led them out! God is patient with us when we are slow to leave what is wrong, and he takes our hand.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to change a bad habit.
family.ask: Ask: “What bad habit do we need God's help to leave behind?”

illus: An illustration

A young man in Muvattupuzha had promised himself every Lent for five years that he would stop gambling on his phone. Every year he lingered: next week, after this match, after this bonus. This Lent his father, without a word of blame, sat with him one evening and helped him delete the apps, then gave him his old basic phone for the rest of the Fast. The son was angry for two days. On the third he said: I needed someone to take my hand. I could not walk out by myself.

pm.open: Merciful Lord, we linger. Take us by the hand and lead us out. Amen.
share: But he lingered (Genesis 19:16). Where do I linger?
There is no one who is righteous, not even one (Romans 3:10). Do I judge others as if I were righteous?
It is not lawful for you to have her (Matthew 14:4). Where does God ask me to speak the truth?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy and lead us out.
interc: For those caught in addictions who want to be free.
For prophets and truth-tellers in Church and society.
For journalists, judges and all who suffer for speaking the truth.
For those in power, that they may not be enslaved by pride.
For prisoners and those unjustly condemned.
pm.close: Father, you took Lot by the hand and gave John the Baptist the courage to die for the truth. Lead us out of our sins, free us from pride, and make us faithful witnesses to your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt; God remembered Abraham and saved Lot.
We carry the treasure of the Gospel in clay jars, afflicted but not crushed.
Blessed Rani Maria served the poor and was killed in 1995; her family forgave her killer.
2027-02-25.action: Pray today, by name, for someone who has hurt you.
2027-02-25.question: What does my heart keep looking back at?

family.explain: Sister Rani Maria was a nun from Kerala who helped poor families in North India. Some people did not like her helping the poor, and she was killed. But her family forgave the man who killed her, and he became sorry and changed his life. That is the power of Jesus' love.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for all who help the poor.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to forgive, like Rani Maria's family did?”

illus: An illustration

A potter in Thrissur showed a group of schoolchildren a cracked clay lamp. He filled it with oil, lit the wick and turned off the lights. The crack let out thin lines of light across the dark room. He said: a perfect lamp shows only one flame. A cracked one lights the whole wall. The children were quiet. One girl asked if he would throw it away. He laughed: never. This is the one I light on Good Friday.

pm.open: Lord, you place your treasure in clay jars. Shine through our weakness. Amen.
share: Lot's wife, behind him, looked back (Genesis 19:26). What do I keep looking back at?
God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out (Genesis 19:29). For whom should I keep praying?
Struck down, but not destroyed (2 Corinthians 4:9). Where has God kept me from being destroyed?
pm.resp: Lord, make your life visible in us.
interc: For missionaries in the villages of India and throughout the world.
For the poor and landless, and for all who work for their freedom.
For those who have killed or harmed others, that they may repent like Samandar Singh.
For families of victims of violence, that they may find the grace to forgive.
For religious sisters, especially the Franciscan Clarist Congregation.
pm.close: Father, you gave Blessed Rani Maria the courage to serve the poor and to lay down her life. Through her prayers, strengthen all who bear your treasure in clay jars, and make forgiveness grow from every wound. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Lot and his daughters, gripped by fear and isolation, fell into sin; yet from Moab came Ruth, ancestor of Jesus.
Whoever judges others condemns himself; God's kindness leads to repentance.
Jesus says: pray to your Father in secret; he knows what you need.
2027-02-26.action: Pray alone today for ten minutes with the door shut.
2027-02-26.question: Do I treat God's patience as permission, or as an invitation to repent?

family.explain: Jesus says that when we pray, we do not need to show off or use lots of words. We can go to a quiet place and talk to God like a child talks to a loving father. God already knows what we need, and he loves to hear us.
family.intention: We pray for people who are lonely and afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “Where is a quiet place in our home where each of us can pray?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Kottarakkara found her teenage daughter shut in her room for days, eating little, scrolling her phone late into the night. The girl would not say what was wrong. Instead of lecturing, the mother began to sit outside the closed door each night with her rosary, saying nothing. On the fifth night the door opened a few inches. The girl said: why are you sitting there? The mother said: so you will know you are not alone in there. That night they talked until two in the morning.

pm.open: Father who sees in secret, we come to you with honest hearts. Lead us to repentance by your kindness. Amen.
share: He was afraid to stay in Zoar (Genesis 19:30). Where has fear led me into a dark place?
In passing judgment on another you condemn yourself (Romans 2:1). Whom have I judged harshly this week?
Your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:8). Do I trust that God knows my needs?
pm.resp: Father, we turn to you.
interc: For people living in isolation, fear and despair.
For families wounded by abuse or by sin within the home.
For those who judge others harshly, and for those who have been judged.
For all who are learning to pray.
For converts and seekers from every nation, like Ruth the Moabite.
pm.close: Father, your kindness is meant to lead us to repentance. Bring light into every cave of fear, give us humble hearts that do not judge, and teach us to meet you in secret prayer. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Out of fear Abraham called Sarah his sister; God protected her and kept Abimelech from sin.
The law is written on human hearts; doers of the law, not hearers only, are righteous.
Jesus asks us to acknowledge him before others, and promises the Holy Spirit's help.
2027-02-27.action: Correct one half-truth you have told.
2027-02-27.question: Where does fear make me hide the truth or hide my faith?

family.explain: Jesus asks us not to be ashamed of him in front of others. Sometimes we are afraid that others will laugh at us if we pray or go to church. But Jesus promises that the Holy Spirit will help us know what to say.
family.intention: We pray for children and young people who are teased because of their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for us to show that we love Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A nursing student from Pathanamthitta working a night shift in Bengaluru was asked by a dying Hindu patient what she whispered at the start of each shift. She hesitated. It would be easier to say: nothing. Then she said: I ask Jesus to help me take care of you. The old man smiled and asked her to say it for him too. She prayed aloud for the first time in her life outside a church. She says she cannot remember the words she used. She thinks someone else gave them to her.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, teach us what to say, and give us courage to acknowledge Jesus. Amen.
share: She is my sister (Genesis 20:2). Where have I used a half-truth to protect myself?
What the law requires is written on their hearts (Romans 2:15). Have I seen more honesty in others than in myself?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Luke 12:8). Where am I ashamed of Christ?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, give us courage.
interc: For those tempted to lie out of fear.
For people of other faiths who follow their conscience with integrity.
For Christians in workplaces and hostels where faith is mocked.
For nurses, doctors and carers who pray for their patients.
For our parish as we approach Knanoitho Sunday.
pm.close: Father, you kept your promise even when Abraham failed, and you write your law on every heart. Make us truthful and brave, and let your Holy Spirit teach us to confess your Son before all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, forty days after Yaldo, Mary and Joseph carry the Child to the Temple in Jerusalem. They come to present him to the Lord, as the Law of Moses required, and they offer two young pigeons, the offering of poor families. The Lord of the Temple enters his own house, carried in his mother's arms.

An old man is waiting there: Simeon, righteous and devout, who had been promised that he would not die before seeing the Messiah. He takes the Child in his arms and sings: “Now, Lord, you are letting your servant go in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation.” A whole lifetime of prayer is rewarded in one moment. And the old prophetess Anna gives thanks and speaks of the Child to everyone.

But Simeon also says to Mary: “A sword will pierce your own soul too.” The Child presented today will one day offer himself on the Cross. Hebrews tells us that Christ entered the true Holy Place with his own blood, obtaining eternal redemption. The joy of Christmas already carries the shadow of the Cross.

On Sunday the Great Fast begins. Let us do what Mary and Joseph did: present ourselves to God, our families, our work, our whole life. Let us learn from Simeon and Anna to wait for the Lord faithfully. And every time we receive Holy Communion, let us say with Simeon: “My eyes have seen your salvation.” Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was a tiny baby, Mary and Joseph took him to the big Temple to give him to God.
An old man called Simeon was there. He had waited all his life to see the Saviour. He held baby Jesus in his arms and said: “Now I am happy; I have seen God's salvation!”
When you receive Jesus or pray to him, you can be happy like Simeon. Let's say: “Jesus, you are my light!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today our Church begins the Great Fast, and it begins it at a wedding. On Kothine Sunday we read how Jesus, at Cana, changed water into wine. Why begin fifty days of fasting with a wedding feast? Because the Fast is not a season of gloom. It is a season of transformation.

At Cana the wine ran out. Mary noticed and said to the servants: “Do whatever he tells you.” That is the best advice for Lent. The servants did a simple thing: they filled the jars with water, up to the brim. And Jesus changed that water into the best wine. In this Fast, let us fill our jars: with prayer, with fasting, with the Word of God, with works of mercy. And let Jesus change the water of our lives into wine.

The prophets tell us what true fasting is. Joel says: “Return to me with all your heart; rend your hearts and not your clothing.” Isaiah says: “Is not this the fast that I choose: to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house?” Fasting from food is not a diet; it makes room in our hearts for God and in our hands for the poor.

Tonight the special prayers of the Fast begin, and tomorrow we celebrate Shubkono, when we ask forgiveness of one another. Let each family make a simple plan: one fast, one prayer, one act of charity. And at the end of these fifty days, at Qyomtho, Jesus will give us the best wine, kept until now: the joy of his Resurrection. Amen.
kids: Children, today Lent begins! And our Gospel is about a wedding party. At the party the wine ran out. Mary said: “Do whatever Jesus tells you.”
The servants filled six big jars with water, and Jesus changed it into wonderful wine! In Lent Jesus wants to change us too: to make us kinder, more patient, more prayerful.
What can you give up this Lent? Sweets? Television? And what good thing can you do? Let's say: “Jesus, change my heart!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in our tradition every Sunday of the Great Fast shows us Christ the physician. Today a leper comes to him. In those days a leper lived outside the village, had to cry “Unclean!” when anyone came near, and could touch no one. This man kneels and says: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”

Then Jesus does something no one else would do. He stretches out his hand and touches him. “I do choose. Be made clean.” By the Law, touching a leper made a person unclean. But with Jesus the opposite happens: his touch makes the leper clean. That is what Lent offers each of us: the touch of Christ on the part of our life we hide from everyone.

Our first reading tells of Naaman, a proud Syrian general with leprosy. The prophet told him simply to wash seven times in the Jordan. He was offended: is that all? But when he humbled himself and obeyed, his flesh became like a child's. Healing needs humility. For us, the Jordan is the sacrament of Confession. It seems too simple. But it heals.

After healing the leper, Jesus withdrew to deserted places to pray. Let us make room for prayer in this Fast, make a good Confession, and reach out to the “lepers” of our time: the sick, the lonely, those everyone avoids. And let us hear Jesus say to us: “I do choose. Be made clean.” Amen.
kids: Children, long ago people with a skin disease called leprosy had to live alone. Nobody would touch them or play with them.
One day a man with leprosy came to Jesus and said: “If you want, you can heal me.” Jesus touched him and said: “I want to. Be healed!” And he was healed!
Is there someone at school whom nobody plays with? Be kind to them, like Jesus. Let's say: “Jesus, make me kind!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, imagine the scene in Capernaum. Jesus is teaching in a house so crowded that no one can get to the door. Four men arrive carrying a friend who cannot walk. What do they do? They climb onto the roof, dig a hole, and lower their friend down right in front of Jesus. They would not give up.

St Mark says: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’” Their faith. Sometimes we cannot bring ourselves to God; others must carry us. And sometimes we are called to carry others: a son who has left the Church, a friend in addiction, a neighbour in despair. Our prayer can open the roof.

Everyone expected Jesus to heal the man's legs. He began with his sins. The deepest paralysis is not in our legs but in our hearts: sin keeps us from walking towards God and others. Only God can forgive sins, said the scribes. Exactly. And to show that he has that authority, Jesus told the man: “Stand up, take your mat and go home.”

Ezekiel warns of people who hear God's word like a beautiful song and then do nothing. Let us not be like that this Lent. Let us make a good Confession, so that we hear Jesus say: “Your sins are forgiven.” And let us become the four friends who carry others to him. Amen.
kids: Children, four friends wanted to bring their friend who could not walk to Jesus. But the house was full of people!
So they climbed onto the roof, made a hole, and lowered their friend down on a mat right in front of Jesus! Jesus forgave his sins and said: “Stand up and walk!” And he walked!
Good friends help each other come to Jesus. Let's say: “Jesus, help me to be a good friend!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today a mother comes to Jesus. She is not one of his people; she is a Canaanite, a foreigner. Her daughter is suffering terribly. She cries out: “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David!” And Jesus does not answer her a word.

Have you ever felt that? You pray and pray, and heaven seems silent. The disciples even want her sent away. Jesus says he was sent first to Israel. But she does not give up. She kneels and says three simple words: “Lord, help me.” And when Jesus speaks of the children's bread, she answers with amazing humility: “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.”

Jesus is amazed: “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” His silence was not a refusal. It was a school of faith, and she passed with honours. Isaiah had said that God's house would be a house of prayer for all peoples. This foreign mother shows us that no one is outside God's mercy.

This Wednesday we reach the middle of the Fast, and the Cross is set up in our church. Look at it when you feel God is silent. St Paul cries: “Who will rescue me? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord!” Mothers and fathers, keep praying for your children. Don't give up. Say with her: “Lord, help me.” Amen.
kids: Children, a mother came to Jesus because her daughter was very sick. She asked and asked: “Jesus, please help!” At first Jesus did not answer.
But she kept trusting and asking. Jesus said: “Your faith is great!” And her daughter was healed.
When you pray and nothing seems to happen, don't stop! Jesus is listening. Let's say: “Jesus, help me!”

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the Colossians: we have not ceased praying for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will (Colossians 1:9). Before he teaches them anything, he prays for them.

Then he reminds them what God has done: he has rescued us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of his beloved Son, in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins (Colossians 1:13–14). We belong to a new kingdom.

In the Gospel Jesus gives us the prayer of that kingdom, the Our Father. Of all its lines he explains only one: if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14).

Next Monday the Great Fast opens with Shubkono, when we ask one another for forgiveness. Let us use this week to say the Our Father slowly and to make peace with anyone we have not yet forgiven. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus gave us his own prayer, the Our Father. When we say it, we ask God to forgive us, and we promise to forgive others too. Is there someone you need to forgive today?

homily: Dear friends, yesterday Jesus was carried into the temple. Today we honour the two old people who were waiting for him: Simeon, righteous and devout, on whom the Holy Spirit rested, and Anna, the widow of eighty-four (Luke 2:25, 37).

Simeon had been promised that he would not see death before he saw the Lord’s Messiah. He came into the temple guided by the Spirit, and the promise was kept. God does not forget those who wait for him.

Anna never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day. When she saw the child she began to praise God and to speak about him to all who were looking for redemption (Luke 2:37–38). Her prayer turned into proclamation.

Paul prays that Christ may dwell in our hearts through faith, as we are being rooted and grounded in love (Ephesians 3:17). As the Fast draws near, let us learn from Simeon and Anna to pray with patience, and thank God for the elders who pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Simeon and Anna were very old, and they waited all their lives to see Jesus. When they saw the baby, they were full of joy! Pray today for your grandparents.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish (Romans 1:14). The gospel he received is a debt he owes to everyone he meets.
