Then he says: I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith (Romans 1:16). Our faith is not a private hobby; it is God's own power.
Jesus does not hide the cost: the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life (Matthew 7:14). We pass through it only by leaving behind what does not fit.

St John de Britto left a noble life in Lisbon, lived as a poor teacher among the Tamil people, and was beheaded at Oriyur in 1693. Let us ask him for courage to pay our debt of the gospel, without shame, wherever we are. Amen.
kids: Children, St John de Britto came from far away Portugal to tell the people of Tamil Nadu about Jesus. He was never ashamed of Jesus. Can you make the sign of the cross before your meal today, even at school?

homily: Dear friends, Paul reminds us that Israel passed through the sea, ate the manna and drank from the rock, and the rock was Christ. Yet most of them fell in the wilderness (1 Corinthians 10:4–5).
These things were written down to instruct us. So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall (1 Corinthians 10:11–12). Grace is not a charm; it calls for watchfulness.
But Paul adds at once: God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out (1 Corinthians 10:13).

Jesus tells us not to be surprised if the world hates us: it hated him first (John 15:18). On this Friday, let us pray for persecuted Christians, and enter the coming Fast watchful and full of trust. Amen.
kids: Children, sometimes it is hard to do what is right. But God is faithful! He never gives us a test that is too big, and he always shows us a way out. Ask him for help when you are tempted.

homily: Dear friends, the rich man in the parable had a good harvest and a simple plan: bigger barns and a comfortable life. He spoke only to his own soul (Luke 12:18–19).
God said to him: You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be? (Luke 12:20). His barn had no door to God or to the poor.
Paul tells Timothy to command the rich not to hope in uncertain riches but in God, and to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share (1 Timothy 6:17–18).
Tomorrow the Great Fast begins in our Sunday worship, and it is also Catholicos Day. Let us open our barns: fasting with almsgiving, so that we may be rich toward God. Amen.
kids: Children, a rich man built bigger and bigger barns for himself, but forgot God and the hungry. During the Great Fast, can you save something and share it with someone who needs it?

homily: Dear friends, today the Great Fast begins, and our Church opens it with Shubkono, asking forgiveness of one another. Paul says: be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you (Ephesians 4:32).

Abram, old and childless, is told: look toward heaven and count the stars; so shall your descendants be. He believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness (Genesis 15:5–6). The Fast begins with faith.
Jesus fasts forty days in the wilderness and answers the tempter: one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4).

So let us begin: trusting like Abram, forgiving one another as we did at Shubkono, and feeding each day on God's word. A fast without love is only hunger; a fast with love becomes a road to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, today the Great Fast begins! Before we give up sweets or meat, Jesus asks us to say sorry and forgive. Is there someone you can hug and say sorry to today?

homily: Dear friends, Abram believed God and yet asked: how am I to know? God answered with a covenant. Abram prepared the sacrifice, and when birds of prey came down on the carcasses, Abram drove them away (Genesis 15:8, 11).
Our Fast is an offering, and birds of prey come to snatch it: distraction, discouragement, the voice that says it is useless. Like Abram, we must keep watch.
But we do not keep watch in fear. There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:1). The Spirit of life dwells in us.
And Jesus says: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). His sacrifice saves us; ours is only to stay close to him and listen to his voice. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is the Good Shepherd. He knows your name, he takes care of you, and he even gave his life for you. In the Fast, let us listen to his voice by reading the Bible.

homily: Dear friends, the covenant with Abram was sealed at night: a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between the pieces (Genesis 15:17). God alone passed through. His promise rests on his faithfulness, not ours.
Paul says: not that I have already reached the goal; but forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on (Philippians 3:12–14). The Fast is our pressing on.
Jesus asks his disciples: but who do you say that I am? Peter answers: the Messiah of God (Luke 9:20). Every Christian must give that answer personally.

Today our Church thanks God for 10 February 2005, when it was raised to a Major Archiepiscopal Church in communion with the See of Peter. Let us pray for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and Synod, and press on together, confessing Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked: who do you say I am? Peter said: you are the Christ! Today our Church says thank you to God for making us a big family together with the Pope. Can you say to Jesus today: you are my Lord?

homily: Dear friends, Sarai tried to keep God's promise her own way. She gave Hagar to Abram, and the household broke: contempt, blame, harshness, and a slave-girl running into the wilderness (Genesis 16:2–6).
Paul shows a different way: set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth, for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:2–3).
Mary lived that way. She sang: he has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant; he has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly (Luke 1:48, 52).

At Lourdes in 1858 she came to Bernadette, a poor sick girl, and the sick have gone there ever since. On this World Day of the Sick, let us pray for the sick, visit them, and magnify the Lord with Mary. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary sang a beautiful song: God loves the little ones! At Lourdes she came to a poor girl, Bernadette. Today, say a Hail Mary for someone who is sick.

homily: Dear friends, Hagar ran away into the wilderness. The angel of the Lord found her by a spring and asked: where have you come from and where are you going? (Genesis 16:8). In this first week of the Fast, God asks us the same.
God heard her affliction, and Hagar named him: You are El-roi, the God who sees (Genesis 16:11, 13). No one is invisible to God.
Paul says that God's law is written even on the hearts of those who have not heard it, and their conscience bears witness (Romans 2:15). In the Fast we let God's light into our secret thoughts.

And Jesus says: everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God (Luke 12:8). On this Friday, let us not hide our faith, and let us trust the Spirit to teach us what to say. Amen.
kids: Children, Hagar was alone in the desert, but God found her! She called him “the God who sees me.” God sees you too, always, and he loves you.

homily: Dear friends, God says to Abram: I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be blameless. And he gives him a new name, Abraham, father of a multitude (Genesis 17:1, 5). The Fast is a time to walk again in God's sight.
God shapes us by his word: the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart (Hebrews 4:12).

But Jesus warns: not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven. Everyone who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock (Matthew 7:21, 24).

Today we remember Mar Aprem, who built on the word with his hymns; Mar Theodore, who built on it with his blood; and the Prophet Haggai, who called the people to rebuild God's house. Let us pray the Prayer of St Ephrem each day of this Fast and build on rock. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: build your house on the rock, not on the sand! When we listen to Jesus and do what he says, we are strong like a house on a rock. St Ephrem wrote beautiful songs about Jesus. Can you sing a hymn to Jesus today?

homily: Dear friends, God told Abraham to mark every man in his household with the sign of the covenant: so shall my covenant be in your flesh an everlasting covenant (Genesis 17:13). God's promise was meant to be carried in the body, not only in the mind.

In Christ the sign is deeper. Moses foretold it: the Lord your God will circumcise your heart (Deuteronomy 30:6). In baptism we were marked for God, and in the Fast we let him cut away what still does not belong to him.

Paul shows us the marks of a covenant life: devote yourselves to prayer, keeping alert in it with thanksgiving; let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt (Colossians 4:2, 6). Fasting that makes us irritable has not yet reached the heart.

And Jesus says: do not worry. Look at the birds of the air; consider the lilies of the field. Strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well (Matthew 6:26, 28, 33). Let us give our worries to the Father this week and pray for Mathews Mar Pachomios. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: look at the birds! They do not go shopping, but God feeds them. Look at the flowers! They do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. God loves you much more than birds and flowers, so you do not need to be afraid. Tell God your worries tonight.

homily: Dear friends, God promised Abraham a son by Sarah, and Abraham fell on his face and laughed: can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? (Genesis 17:17). God did not take back the promise. He named the child Isaac, he laughs.

Abraham also prayed: O that Ishmael might live in your sight! And God answered: as for Ishmael, I have heard you; I will bless him (Genesis 17:18, 20). God's plan is larger than our hopes and kinder than our fears.

Paul says that we too were given life when it was impossible: you were dead through the trespasses and sins... but God, who is rich in mercy, made us alive together with Christ. By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God (Ephesians 2:1, 4–5, 8).

Grace bears fruit. Jesus says: you will know them by their fruits; every good tree bears good fruit (Matthew 7:16–17). Our fasting does not earn God's love; it opens us to receive it, so that we may bear the fruit he has prepared. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham was a hundred years old and Sarah was ninety when God promised them a baby. Abraham laughed! But God kept his promise, and baby Isaac was born. Nothing is impossible for God. God's love is a gift; we cannot buy it, only say thank you.

homily: Dear friends, Genesis says it twice: that very day. Abraham, ninety-nine years old, obeyed God's command that very day, beginning with himself and his household (Genesis 17:23, 26).
Delay is a quiet enemy of the Fast. We mean to pray, to confess, to forgive, to give; and the days slip by. The Psalmist says: I hurry and do not delay to keep your commandments (Psalm 119:60).

In the Gospel one man promises: I will follow you wherever you go. Another says: first let me go and bury my father. Jesus answers: the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head... Follow me (Matthew 8:19–22). Nothing may come before him, not even good things.
Why is he worth it? Because in him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge (Colossians 2:3). Let us not wait for a better season. Today is the day to follow. Amen.
kids: Children, when God asked Abraham to do something, he did it that very day! When Jesus says follow me, let us not say later, later. Is there something good your mum or dad asked you to do? Do it today, with a smile.

homily: Dear friends, on a hot afternoon Abraham saw three men near his tent. He ran to meet them, bowed down, and said: my lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant (Genesis 18:2–3). He promised a little bread and gave a feast.
The Fathers saw in these three guests a sign of the Holy Trinity. St Ambrose says Abraham saw three and worshipped one (in substance). The God of glory came as a guest to an old man's tent.
Now God makes his home in us: we are the temple of the living God; I will live in them and walk among them (2 Corinthians 6:16). A temple must be kept free of idols.

And God invites us to his Son's wedding banquet, good and bad alike. But he asks: friend, how did you get in here without a wedding robe? (Matthew 22:12). That robe is charity. On this Thursday, let us prepare it for the banquet of the altar. Amen.
kids: Children, Abraham had three visitors, and he ran to welcome them! He gave them water to wash their feet and cooked them a big meal. When a visitor comes to your house, you can be like Abraham: say welcome, offer a chair and a glass of water.

homily: Dear friends, Sarah heard behind the tent that she would have a son, and she laughed to herself. The Lord asked: why did Sarah laugh? Is anything too wonderful for the Lord? (Genesis 18:13–14).

She denied it, for she was afraid. He said: oh yes, you did laugh (Genesis 18:15). God does not condemn her; he simply keeps his word. Many of us carry such a hidden laugh, a quiet doubt that God can still do something new.

Paul shows where hope is found: I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord (Philippians 3:8). He wanted to share Christ's sufferings so as to know the power of his resurrection.
And Jesus promises: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand (John 10:28). On this Friday, let us place our doubts and losses into that hand. Amen.
kids: Children, Sarah laughed when God said she would have a baby, because she was very old. But God asked: is anything too wonderful for me? And baby Isaac was born! Jesus holds you in his hand, and nobody can take you away from him.

homily: Dear friends, the Lord said: shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do? I have chosen him, that he may charge his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord by doing righteousness and justice (Genesis 18:17, 19). God trusts Abraham as a friend, and expects faith to be passed on at home.
God also hears the outcry against Sodom: I must go down and see (Genesis 18:20–21). The cry of the oppressed reaches heaven.

Paul says we were once foolish and led astray, but when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:3–5). So we are to be gentle and courteous to everyone.

And Jesus says: do not be afraid, little flock. Sell your possessions, and give alms. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Luke 12:32–34). As we end this second week of the Fast, let us move our treasure, and our heart, toward God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus calls us his little flock, like little sheep. He says: do not be afraid! God wants to give you his kingdom. When we share our things with poor people, we are storing treasure in heaven. What can you share this week?

homily: Dear friends, today we honour the See of St Peter at Antioch, where the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26). Jesus prayed for Peter that his faith might not fail, and told him to strengthen his brothers (Luke 22:32).

Hebrews says: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:7–8). Shepherds come and go; Christ remains.

A true shepherd stands before God for his people. Abraham remained standing before the Lord and asked: will you indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked? (Genesis 18:22–23). From fifty to ten he pleaded, and God listened.

Jesus asks: who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household? (Matthew 24:45). Let us pray for the Pope and our bishops, and let each of us be faithful in the place God has given us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus chose St Peter to be the leader of his apostles and said: strengthen your brothers. Today we pray for the Pope and our bishops, who take care of the Church like shepherds. Abraham prayed for a whole city. You can pray for your town tonight!

homily: Dear friends, today we remember Mar Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, a disciple of St John. When the proconsul ordered him to curse Christ, he answered that he had served Christ for eighty-six years and had never been wronged; how could he blaspheme his King and Saviour? (in substance).

Paul tells us the secret of such faithfulness: suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts (Romans 5:3–5).

In Sodom Lot welcomed God's messengers, but violence surrounded his house. It was the guests who saved him: the men inside reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them, and shut the door (Genesis 19:10). God reaches out to pull us from danger.

And Jesus says: come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me (Matthew 11:28–29). Let us bring our burdens to him in this Fast, as Polycarp did all his life. Amen.
kids: Children, St Polycarp was a very old bishop who loved Jesus. Bad men told him to say Jesus was not good. He said: Jesus has been good to me all my life! He was brave because he loved Jesus. Jesus says: come to me when you are tired, and I will help you.

homily: Dear friends, the angels urged Lot to leave Sodom. But he lingered; so the men seized him and his wife and his two daughters by the hand, the Lord being merciful to him, and they brought him out (Genesis 19:16).
We too linger over what we know we must leave. God is patient: he takes us by the hand. But he also says: flee for your life; do not look back (Genesis 19:17).
Paul reminds us that no one escapes by his own goodness: there is no one who is righteous, not even one (Romans 3:10). We all need the hand of mercy.

Today we remember the finding of the head of St John the Baptist. He told Herod: it is not lawful for you to have her (Matthew 14:4), and died for it. Herod lingered between conscience and pride and chose pride. John did not linger. Let us not linger either. Amen.
kids: Children, Lot was slow to leave the bad city, so the angels took his hand and led him out. God is kind and patient with us too. St John the Baptist was brave and always told the truth, even to the king. Ask Jesus to make you brave to tell the truth.

homily: Dear friends, the Lord rained fire on Sodom. Lot's wife, behind him, looked back, and she became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). She was already outside, but her heart had stayed behind. Jesus says: remember Lot's wife (Luke 17:32).

Yet the reading ends with mercy: God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow (Genesis 19:29). Lot was saved because Abraham had prayed. Our prayer for others is never wasted.

Today we remember Blessed Rani Maria, a sister from Kerala who served the poor in Madhya Pradesh and was killed on 25 February 1995. Paul could have been speaking of her: we have this treasure in clay jars... struck down, but not destroyed (2 Corinthians 4:7, 9).

Jesus warned: I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). Rani Maria went, and her family forgave her killer, who repented. Let us ask her prayers for the courage to serve and the grace to forgive. Amen.
kids: Children, Sister Rani Maria was a brave nun from Kerala. She went far away to help poor families. A man hurt her and she died. But her family forgave him, and he became sorry and good. Jesus' love is stronger than hate. Can you forgive someone today?

homily: Dear friends, today's reading tells a sad story. Lot, saved from Sodom, went to live in a cave with his daughters, afraid and alone (Genesis 19:30). Fear and isolation led to grave sin. Scripture does not praise it; it warns us.

Yet God's plan did not end in the cave. From Moab came Ruth, who said: your people shall be my people, and your God my God (Ruth 1:16). She became an ancestor of David and of Jesus. God can bring good even from the darkest places.
Paul warns us not to judge: in passing judgment on another you condemn yourself. Do you not realize that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance? (Romans 2:1, 4).

And Jesus teaches us to pray in secret: go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:6, 8). On this Friday, let us bring our hidden darkness to the Father who sees in secret. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says you do not need to use big words when you pray. You can go to a quiet place and talk to God like a friend. God already knows what you need, and he loves to listen to you. Try it tonight before you sleep.

homily: Dear friends, Abraham, the friend of God, became afraid in Gerar and said of Sarah: she is my sister (Genesis 20:2). A half-truth told in fear put God's promise at risk.

But God guarded his promise. He spoke to King Abimelech in a dream: yes, I know that you did this in the integrity of your heart; furthermore it was I who kept you from sinning against me (Genesis 20:6). And he still called Abraham a prophet who would pray for the king. God does not discard his weak servants.
Paul says the law is written on the hearts of Gentiles too, and their conscience bears witness. It is not the hearers of the law who are righteous in God's sight, but the doers (Romans 2:13, 15).

Jesus asks for courage: everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God. And he promises: the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say (Luke 12:8, 12). As the third week of the Fast ends, let us ask the Spirit for truthful lips and brave hearts. Amen.
kids: Children, even Abraham was sometimes afraid and did not tell the whole truth. But God still loved him and helped him. Jesus wants us to be brave and tell the truth, and not be ashamed of him. The Holy Spirit will help you. Try saying a prayer before lunch at school this week!

intro: Theme: “The Lord comes to his Temple.”
Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring Jesus to the Temple. There two elderly people, Simeon and Anna, recognise him. The Lord whom Israel sought has come to his house.

sub: The Law allowed those who could not afford a lamb to offer two birds.
Mary and Joseph bring the offering of the poor; yet they carry the true Lamb.
God values not the size of our gift but the heart that offers it.
q: If she cannot afford a sheep, she shall take two turtledoves or two pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering.
They offered a sacrifice according to what is stated in the law of the Lord, “a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
points.apply: Offer yourself, your family and your work at the altar today, however small it seems.

sub: Malachi promised: the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Simeon, righteous and devout, waited for the consolation of Israel; the Spirit led him to the Child.
Holding Jesus, he sings: now I can depart in peace. Faithful old age sees salvation.
q: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.

Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
points.apply: Honour the elderly in your family and parish; listen to their faith.

points.h: A sign that will be opposed
sub: Isaiah spoke of a stone of stumbling as well as a sanctuary.
Simeon tells Mary that the Child will be a sign opposed, and a sword will pierce her soul.
Following Christ means choosing a side; Mary shows us how to stand faithful in sorrow.
q: He will become a sanctuary, a stone one strikes against; for both houses of Israel he will become a rock one stumbles over.

This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.
points.apply: Ask Mary for courage to remain faithful to Christ when it costs you.

concl: The Light of the nations entered the Temple in the arms of his mother.
Let us receive him as Simeon did, and let our lives be an offering in his house.
2027-02-02.resolve: Pray Simeon's song (Luke 2:29–32) each night before sleep this week.

intro: Theme: “The Fast begins at a wedding.”

Our Great Fast does not begin with ashes but with a wedding at Cana. The Church tells us that Lent is not sadness but the joyful return of the Bride to the Bridegroom, who turns the water of our efforts into the wine of his grace.

sub: Joel calls: return with fasting, weeping and mourning; rend your hearts, not your clothing.
At Cana Mary notices: “They have no wine.” Lent begins by admitting what we lack.
Her counsel is the programme of the Fast: “Do whatever he tells you.”
q: Yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing.
When the wine gave out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” … His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
points.apply: Name the “wine” that has run out in your life (joy, peace, love) and bring it to Jesus.

sub: Fasting from food has meaning when it frees us for justice and charity.
Isaiah: share your bread, shelter the homeless, clothe the naked.
Jesus: fast in secret; the Father who sees in secret will reward you.
q: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free … Is it not to share your bread with the hungry?
But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face, so that your fasting may be seen not by others but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Set aside the money saved by fasting for the poor.

sub: The servants fill the jars to the brim; Jesus does the rest.
The best wine is kept for last: God's grace exceeds our efforts.
After the flood God gave a covenant sign; at Cana Jesus gives the first sign of the new covenant.
q: I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
“You have kept the good wine until now.” Jesus did this, the first of his signs, in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.
points.apply: Fill your “jars” this Lent: daily prayer, Scripture, fasting and charity, and trust Jesus to transform them.

concl: The Fast is a wedding feast in preparation: the Bridegroom is coming to his Passion and Resurrection.
Let us return with all our hearts, fast as God desires, and let him change our water into wine.
2027-02-07.resolve: Choose three Lenten practices (prayer, fasting, almsgiving) and write them down today.

intro: Theme: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”

The Great Fast leads us through Sundays of healing. The first is the leper: a man shut out of community, who dares to come to Jesus. Leprosy is an image of sin, which isolates us from God and from one another.

sub: The Law made the leper live alone, outside the camp.
Sin does the same: it breaks our communion with God, family and Church.
The leper does not hide; he falls on his face before Jesus and asks.
q: He shall remain unclean as long as he has the disease; he is unclean. He shall live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
There was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he bowed with his face to the ground and begged him, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
points.apply: Name the sin that isolates you, and bring it humbly to the Lord.

sub: No one touched lepers; Jesus stretches out his hand and touches him.
His answer is clear: “I do choose.” God wants our healing.
The Psalmist knows the connection: “heal me, for I have sinned against you.”
q: As for me, I said, “O LORD, be gracious to me; heal me, for I have sinned against you.”
Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
points.apply: Reach out this week to someone others avoid: the sick, the shamed, the lonely.

sub: Naaman wanted a dramatic cure; he was told simply to wash in the Jordan.
When he obeyed, his flesh became like a child's.
Jesus sends the healed man to the priest: today Christ heals our sins through the priest in Confession.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
“Go,” he said, “and show yourself to the priest, and, as Moses commanded, make an offering for your cleansing, for a testimony to them.”
points.apply: Make a good confession during this Great Fast.

concl: What the leper said, we can say: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
Christ chooses. Let us come to him, let him touch us, and go home clean.
2027-02-14.resolve: Prepare an examination of conscience this week and go to confession.

intro: Theme: “When Jesus saw their faith.”
A paralysed man cannot reach Jesus by himself. Four friends carry him, break open a roof and lower him down. Jesus sees their faith, forgives the man's sins and raises him up.

sub: Aaron and Hur held up the weary hands of Moses until the battle was won.
Four friends carry the paralytic and find a way through the roof.
The Church is a community where we carry one another to Jesus by prayer and help.
q: Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
And when they could not bring him to Jesus because of the crowd, they removed the roof above him; and after having dug through it, they let down the mat on which the paralytic lay.
points.apply: Carry one person to Jesus this week: pray for them by name and help them practically.

sub: Jesus first says: “Son, your sins are forgiven.” The deepest paralysis is sin.
The Psalmist blesses God who forgives all iniquity and heals all diseases.
In the sacrament of Reconciliation Christ still speaks these words through his priest.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits—who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Thank God for the times he has forgiven you, and forgive someone who has hurt you.

sub: God takes no pleasure in the death of the sinner, but wants him to turn and live.
Jesus shows his authority: “Stand up, take your mat and go to your home.”
The healed man walks out before all; forgiveness gives new life and new strength for daily duties.
q: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live.
“I say to you, stand up, take your mat and go to your home.” And he stood up, and immediately took the mat and went out before all of them.
points.apply: Take up one duty you have been avoiding at home, and do it with new heart.

concl: Faith carried the man, mercy forgave him, power raised him.
Let us be friends who carry others, sinners who accept forgiveness, and disciples who rise and walk.
2027-02-21.resolve: Pray each day this week for one person who is spiritually or physically “paralysed”.

intro: Theme: “Woman, great is your faith!”

A foreign mother cries out for her daughter. Jesus is silent; the disciples want her sent away; she is answered with a hard word. Yet she persists, and Jesus praises her great faith. Her story teaches us how to pray when God seems silent.

sub: She is a Canaanite, an outsider, yet she calls Jesus “Lord, Son of David”.
She brings her daughter's suffering as her own: “Have mercy on me.”
Isaiah's prayer is hers and ours: “O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you.”
q: O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be our arm every morning, our salvation in the time of trouble.
Just then a Canaanite woman from that region came out and started shouting, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is tormented by a demon.”
points.apply: Pray this week for children in trouble: sick, addicted, lost or far from God.

sub: “He did not answer her at all.” God's silence is not his absence.
The Psalmist also cried: “How long, O LORD?”
She does not leave; she kneels: “Lord, help me.” Persistent, humble prayer grows deeper through testing.
q: How long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
But he did not answer her at all … But she came and knelt before him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
points.apply: Do not stop praying for the intention you have carried longest.

points.h: Great faith and bread for all
sub: She accepts the hard word humbly and turns it into hope: even the dogs eat the crumbs.
Jesus praises her: “Woman, great is your faith!” and her daughter is healed.
Isaiah foresaw it: foreigners gathered into God's house of prayer for all peoples.
q: These I will bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer … for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
She said, “Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.” Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.”
points.apply: Welcome a stranger or someone from another community in your parish or workplace.

concl: The Canaanite woman shows us humble, persistent, confident faith.
Let us keep praying for those we love, and never doubt that the Lord's table has bread for all.
2027-02-28.resolve: Pray a decade of the Rosary each day this week for a child or young person in difficulty.

intro: Theme: “Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
A week before the Great Fast, the Church puts the Lord's Prayer in our hands.

points.h: Filled with the knowledge of his will
q: Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Let your good spirit lead me on a level path.
For this reason, since the day we heard it, we have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of God’s will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
points.apply: Pray by name today for three people you love.

sub: His name, his kingdom, his will first.
q: Yet, O Lord, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly, once in the morning and once at night.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
points.apply: Make peace with one person before the Fast begins.

concl: We have been moved from darkness into the kingdom of the Son.
The prayer of that kingdom asks forgiveness and promises it.
2027-02-01.resolve: Before next Monday, forgive one person from the heart.

intro: Theme: “She came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child.”
Two old people who waited, prayed and were not disappointed.

q: Comfort, O comfort my people, says your God.
Now there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon; this man was righteous and devout, looking forward to the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit rested on him.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit each morning this week to guide your steps.

points.h: Fasting and prayer night and day
q: In old age they still produce fruit; they are always green and full of sap,
then as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.
points.apply: Plan one concrete act of prayer and fasting for the Great Fast.

q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love.
points.apply: Thank an elder who taught you the faith.

concl: God keeps his promises to those who wait for him.
Prayer rooted in love becomes witness.
2027-02-03.resolve: Visit or call one elderly person this week.

intro: Theme: “I am not ashamed of the gospel.”
Paul's debt to all, the narrow gate, and a martyr of our own land.

sub: The gospel is not ours to keep.
Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish
points.apply: Pray for one person who does not yet know Christ, and look for a chance to speak.

q: I will also speak of your decrees before kings, and shall not be put to shame;
For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross openly before meals this week.

q: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
For the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and there are few who find it.
points.apply: Choose one costly right thing today instead of the easy wrong one.

concl: The gospel is a debt we owe to everyone.
The martyrs show that the narrow gate opens on life.
2027-02-04.resolve: Pray this week for the Church in Tamil Nadu and for missionaries in India.

intro: Theme: “If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.”
Paul's warning from the wilderness and Jesus' word to the persecuted.

q: Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall.
points.apply: Name one temptation you will guard against during the Fast.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength,
points.apply: In your next temptation, stop and ask God to show you the way out.

q: More in number than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause;
If the world hates you, be aware that it hated me before it hated you.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians each Friday of the Great Fast.

concl: Grace received must be guarded with watchfulness.
God is faithful to those who suffer for his name.
2027-02-05.resolve: Choose one Friday act of prayer for the persecuted Church and keep it through the Fast.

intro: Theme: “Not rich toward God.”
On the eve of the Great Fast, the Church puts almsgiving beside fasting.

q: Put no confidence in extortion, and set no vain hopes on robbery; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.

As for those who in the present age are rich, command them not to be haughty, or to set their hopes on the uncertainty of riches, but rather on God who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment.
points.apply: Thank God today for three things money cannot buy.

q: Do not be afraid when some become rich, when the wealth of their houses increases. For when they die they will carry nothing away; their wealth will not go down after them.
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be?’
points.apply: Decide what you will give away this Lent, not only what you will give up.

sub: A good foundation for the future.
The life that really is life.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and will be repaid in full.
They are to do good, to be rich in good works, generous, and ready to share,
points.apply: Give generously at the Catholicos Day collection tomorrow.

concl: A life that stores up only for itself is foolish before God.
Generosity is the true wealth that lasts.
2027-02-06.resolve: Keep a Lenten box for the poor at home from tomorrow until Pesaha.

intro: Theme: “Forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”
The Great Fast opens with faith, forgiveness and the word of God.

q: After these things the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, “Do not be afraid, Abram, I am your shield; your reward shall be very great.”
For what does the scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.”
points.apply: Bring one fear to God in prayer each day of this first week.

sub: Not letting the sun go down on anger.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the Lord.
Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger,
points.apply: Make peace with one person before sunset today.

sub: Angels came and waited on him.
q: He humbled you by letting you hunger, then by feeding you with manna, with which neither you nor your ancestors were acquainted, in order to make you understand that one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
But he answered, “It is written, ‘One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
points.apply: Read one Gospel chapter every day of the Fast.

concl: The Fast begins with trust in God's promise and peace with one another.
Jesus has gone before us into the wilderness and overcome.
2027-02-08.resolve: Keep the Fast with a forgiving heart and a daily portion of Scripture.

intro: Theme: “The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.”
Abram keeps watch over the sacrifice; Christ lays down his life for us.

points.h: Driving away the birds of prey
q: And when birds of prey came down on the carcasses, Abram drove them away.
And thus Abraham, having patiently endured, obtained the promise.
points.apply: Name and drive away the distraction that most steals your prayer.

sub: Set free by the Spirit of life.
The mind set on the Spirit.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Make a good confession during this first part of the Fast.

sub: He does not run from the wolf.
q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord God.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own and my own know me,
points.apply: Pray daily in the Fast for one person who has left the flock.

concl: Our Fast is an offering we guard with patient watching.
The Good Shepherd has already laid down his life for us.
2027-02-09.resolve: Spend ten quiet minutes each day of the Fast with the day's Gospel.

intro: Theme: “But who do you say that I am?”
God's faithful covenant, Paul's pressing on, and Peter's confession, on the anniversary of our Church's Major Archiepiscopal status.

q: On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates,
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to the promise.
points.apply: Recall three moments when God was faithful to you, and thank him.

q: Do not remember the former things, or consider the things of old. I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it?
forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Let go of one past failure that is holding back your Fast.

sub: What the crowds say, what you say.
q: I will tell of the decree of the Lord: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “The Messiah of God.”
points.apply: Pray daily this week for the Pope and our Major Archbishop-Catholicos.

concl: God's covenant rests on his faithfulness.
Our Church, in Peter's communion, presses on confessing Christ.
2027-02-10.resolve: Write your own confession of who Jesus is, and pray it each morning of the Fast.

intro: Theme: “He has looked with favor on the lowliness of his servant.”
A plan made without God, a life hidden with Christ, and the song of the lowly on the World Day of the Sick.

sub: Sarai runs ahead of the promise.
q: Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the Lord!
Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth,
points.apply: Bring one hurried decision to God in prayer before acting.

q: You who live in the shelter of the Most High, who abide in the shadow of the Almighty,
for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
points.apply: Do one good deed today that no one will see.

sub: The sick are God's favoured ones.
q: He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes and inherit a seat of honor.
He has brought down the powerful from their thrones, and lifted up the lowly;
points.apply: Visit or call a sick person this week.

concl: God's promises are kept in God's way and time.
He looks with favour on the lowly and the sick.
2027-02-11.resolve: Pray the Magnificat each evening of this week for the sick.

intro: Theme: “Everyone who acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man also will acknowledge before the angels of God.”
The God who sees Hagar, the law written on the heart, and courage to confess Christ.

sub: Found by a spring in the wilderness.
Where have you come from, where are you going?
q: So she named the Lord who spoke to her, “You are El-roi”; for she said, “Have I really seen God and remained alive after seeing him?”
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in hidden prayer each day of the Fast.

q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
They show that what the law requires is written on their hearts, to which their own conscience also bears witness;
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience and go to confession.

sub: The Spirit teaches what to say.
q: The Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.
points.apply: Speak of your faith openly in one conversation this week.

concl: No one is invisible to the God who sees.
He who sees our hearts gives us courage to confess his Son.
2027-02-12.resolve: Make a good confession before the middle of the Fast.

intro: Theme: “Hears these words of mine and acts on them.”
At the end of the first week of the Fast: Abraham's new name, the living word, and the saints who built on rock.

sub: A new name, a new life.
q: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram, and said to him, “I am God Almighty; walk before me, and be blameless.
Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become “the father of many nations,” according to what was said, “So numerous shall your descendants be.”
points.apply: Begin each day of next week with a short act of placing yourself before God.

q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Pray the Prayer of St Ephrem every day of the Fast.

q: Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
points.apply: Choose one word of Jesus heard this week and put it into practice.

concl: God gives a new name to those who walk before him.
The saints built on the rock of his word by doing it.
2027-02-13.resolve: Pray the Prayer of St Ephrem each day and act on one word of the Gospel each week of the Fast.

intro: Theme: “Strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
A covenant marked in the body, a life seasoned with salt, a heart set free from worry.

sub: Every male, from eight days old.
Circumcision of the heart in baptism.
q: Moreover, the Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you will love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, in order that you may live.
In him also you were circumcised with a spiritual circumcision, by putting off the body of the flesh in the circumcision of Christ;
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises quietly each morning this week.

q: A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer everyone.
points.apply: Fast from one habit of harsh or complaining speech for the rest of the week.

sub: Today's trouble is enough for today.
q: Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
points.apply: Each night this week, name one worry and hand it to the Father before sleep.

concl: The covenant is cut into the heart, not only the body.
Those who seek the kingdom first are freed from the tyranny of worry.
2027-02-15.resolve: Each day of this week, pray before anything else: Father, your kingdom first.

intro: Theme: “By grace you have been saved through faith.”
God's impossible gift to Abraham, God's impossible gift to us, and the fruit that grace bears.

sub: “O that Ishmael might live in your sight!”
Isaac: God turns doubt into joy.
q: The nations shall see your vindication, and all the kings your glory; and you shall be called by a new name that the mouth of the Lord will give.
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Bring to God the promise you find hardest to believe, and pray over it each day this week.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
For we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand to be our way of life.
points.apply: Make a good confession this week, receiving mercy as pure gift.

q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit to practise deliberately for the rest of the Fast.

concl: What is impossible for us is the beginning of God's work.
Grace received in faith becomes fruit in good works.
2027-02-16.resolve: Thank God each night of the Fast for one gift you did not earn.

intro: Theme: “Follow me.”
Abraham's prompt obedience, the treasure hidden in Christ, and the call that will not wait.

q: I hurry and do not delay to keep your commandments.
Immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Carry out this week the Lenten resolution you have postponed longest.

q: For the Lord gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
but to those who are the called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
points.apply: Read one chapter of a Gospel every day until Easter.

q: Even the sparrow finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, at your altars, O Lord of hosts, my King and my God.
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts a hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
points.apply: Name the one thing you place before Christ and offer it to him at the next Holy Qurbono.

concl: God's word is best obeyed on the day it is heard.
The one who had nowhere to lay his head is the treasure worth everything.
2027-02-17.resolve: Each day of this week, do at once the first good thing God puts in your heart.

intro: Theme: “We are the temple of the living God.”
God as guest at Mamre, God dwelling in his temple, God as host at the wedding feast.

sub: A little bread, a great feast.
q: He said, “My lord, if I find favor with you, do not pass by your servant.
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Share a meal this week with someone who is alone or a stranger.

points.h: The temple of the living God
sub: God lives and walks among us.
Sons and daughters of the Lord Almighty.
q: And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people.
Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
points.apply: Name one idol in your life and give it up for the rest of the Fast.

sub: Those invited made light of it.
q: I will greatly rejoice in the Lord, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness,
Above all, clothe yourselves with love, which binds everything together in perfect harmony.
points.apply: Be reconciled with one person before your next Holy Qurbono.

concl: The God who came as a guest now dwells in us as his temple.
He invites all to his feast and clothes us in love.
2027-02-18.resolve: Welcome every guest this Fast as if the Lord himself had come to your door.

intro: Theme: “Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?”
Sarah's hidden laugh, Paul's great exchange, and the hand that holds us fast.

q: Ah Lord God! It is you who made the heavens and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm! Nothing is too hard for you.
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Bring your most hopeless situation before God every day of this week.

q: Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire other than you.
More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.
points.apply: Give up one comfort each Friday of the Fast and spend that time before the crucifix.

sub: The Father and I are one.
q: See, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me.
I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand.
points.apply: When fear comes this week, pray: Lord, I am in your hand.

concl: God keeps his word even when we laugh in disbelief.
Those who count all as loss for Christ are held in a hand no one can open.
2027-02-19.resolve: Each Friday of the Fast, spend time before the crucifix and renew your hope in God.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid, little flock.”
A household that keeps the way of the Lord, a mercy that renews, and a heart that follows its treasure.

q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Begin or renew family prayer with Scripture every evening of the Fast.

sub: Not by works, but by mercy.
q: The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
Jesus answered, “Very truly, I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and Spirit.
points.apply: Be gentle and courteous this week to the person you find hardest to bear.

sub: Purses that do not wear out.
q: Prayer with fasting is good, but better than both is almsgiving with righteousness.
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal.
points.apply: Keep a Lenten alms box at home and give its contents to the poor before Easter.

concl: God entrusts his ways to households that will hand them on.
Where our alms go, our hearts follow.
2027-02-20.resolve: Give each week of the Fast what you have saved by fasting.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
On the feast of Peter's See at Antioch: the intercessor, the leaders who spoke God's word, and the faithful servant.

sub: Will you sweep away the righteous?
q: Far be it from you to do such a thing, to slay the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous fare as the wicked! Far be that from you! Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?
First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone,
points.apply: Pray by name each day this week for one town or neighbourhood.

q: Listen to me, you that pursue righteousness, you that seek the Lord. Look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the quarry from which you were dug.
And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
points.apply: Pray daily during the Fast for the Pope, our Catholicos and your bishop.

sub: Found at work when he comes.
q: I will look with favor on the faithful in the land, so that they may live with me; whoever walks in the way that is blameless shall minister to me.
Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
points.apply: Do one duty entrusted to you this week with special faithfulness, as for the Lord.

concl: Shepherds pass; the Christ they serve is the same forever.
Every Christian is called to intercede and to serve faithfully in God's household.
2027-02-22.resolve: Pray each day of the Fast for the shepherds of the Church and for one place that needs God's mercy.

intro: Theme: “Come to me… and I will give you rest.”
On the day of Mar Polycarp: God's hand that pulls us from danger, the hope that does not disappoint, and the rest of Christ.

sub: The guests reach out and shut the door.
q: For he will command his angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one time he rescued you from danger or sin.

q: but those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
and hope does not disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.
points.apply: Offer each hardship this week for Christians who suffer for the faith.

sub: Eighty-six years under the easy yoke.
q: Thus says the Lord: Stand at the crossroads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way lies; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
points.apply: Make a short visit to the Blessed Sacrament each day this week to lay down your burden.

concl: God reaches into our darkest nights to pull us to safety.
Those who carry Christ's yoke, like Polycarp, find it light to the end.
2027-02-23.resolve: Bring your burdens to Christ each day of the Fast, and carry others' burdens with him.

intro: Theme: “The Lord being merciful to him.”
On the day of the finding of John the Baptist's head: the man who lingered, the truth that all have sinned, and the prophet who did not linger.

sub: The sons-in-law thought it a joke.
Seized by the hand in mercy.
q: Seek the Lord while he may be found, call upon him while he is near;
See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Make your Lenten confession this week instead of waiting for Holy Week.

q: They have all gone astray, they are all alike perverse; there is no one who does good, no, not one.
since all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
points.apply: Each time you are tempted to judge someone this week, pray: Lord, have mercy on us both.

sub: A foolish oath at a banquet.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Speak one necessary truth this week, gently and without fear.

concl: God's mercy takes the lingering by the hand.
John, who did not linger, was free even in chains.
2027-02-24.resolve: Leave behind, this week, the sin you have lingered over longest.

intro: Theme: “We have this treasure in clay jars.”
On the memorial of Blessed Rani Maria: the heart that looked back, the prayer that saved, and the treasure that shines through weakness.

q: He is mindful of his covenant forever, of the word that he commanded, for a thousand generations,
points.apply: Remove this week one occasion that keeps drawing your heart back to sin.

sub: So that his life may be visible.
q: Can I not do with you, O house of Israel, just as this potter has done? says the Lord. Just like the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Israel.
but he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”
points.apply: Offer to God this week the weakness you are most ashamed of, and ask him to shine through it.

sub: Struck down on a bus near Indore.
q: Even though you intended to do harm to me, God intended it for good, in order to preserve a numerous people, as he is doing today.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for someone who has harmed you, and do them one good turn if you can.

concl: God remembers those for whom we pray.
In clay jars like Rani Maria, his power overcomes evil with forgiveness.
2027-02-25.resolve: Pray each day of the Fast for one person who has hurt you.

intro: Theme: “God’s kindness is meant to lead you to repentance.”
The cave of fear, the patience of God, and the secret room of prayer.

q: But Ruth said, “Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from following you! Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
and Salmon the father of Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth, and Obed the father of Jesse,
points.apply: Reach out this week to someone who is isolated or afraid.

q: for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
points.apply: For one week, replace every judgment of another with a prayer for them.

sub: Not to be seen by others.
q: Even before a word is on my tongue, O Lord, you know it completely.
Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness; for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but that very Spirit intercedes with sighs too deep for words.
points.apply: Pray ten minutes alone, with the door shut, every day for the rest of the Fast.

concl: Fear and isolation lead into the cave; God's kindness leads out.
The Father who sees in secret meets us in the hidden room of prayer.
2027-02-26.resolve: Pray each day of the Fast in secret, and judge no one.

intro: Theme: “It was I who kept you from sinning against me.”
Abraham's fearful half-truth, the honest conscience of a stranger, and the courage to acknowledge Christ.

sub: A half-truth that endangers the promise.
q: Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who act faithfully are his delight.
Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have stripped off the old self with its practices
points.apply: Examine this week where you use half-truths, and confess them.

q: I the Lord test the mind and search the heart, to give to all according to their ways, according to the fruit of their doings.
whenever our hearts condemn us; for God is greater than our hearts, and he knows everything.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one time he kept you from sin without your knowing.

sub: The Spirit teaches what to say.
The door of mercy is open.
q: You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen,
because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Make one public sign of your faith this week without shame.

concl: God guards his promise even when his friends fail.
The Spirit gives truthful lips and brave hearts to those who ask.
2027-02-27.resolve: Tell the whole truth and acknowledge Christ openly for the rest of the Fast.
